title.zh: 卷十九 列傳第九 謝晦 謝裕 謝方明 謝靈運
title.en: Volume 19 Biographies 9: Xie Hui, Xie Yu, Xie Fangming, Xie Lingyun
title.raw: 卷十九 列傳第九 謝晦 謝裕 謝方明 謝靈運 Volume 19 Biographies 9: Xie Hui, Xie Yu, Xie Fangming, Xie Lingyun

sentences.zh: 谢晦，字宣明，陈郡阳夏人，晋太常裒之玄孙也。

translations.literal: Xie Hui, styled Xuanming, was a man of Yangxia in Chen Commandery, great-great-grandson of Xie Pou, Grand Master of Ceremonies under Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Hui, courtesy name Xuanming, came from Yangxia in Chen Commandery and was the great-great-grandson of Xie Pou, Grand Master of Ceremonies under Jin.

sentences.zh: 裒子奕、据、安、万、铁，并著名前史。

translations.literal: Pou's sons Yi, Ju, An, Wan, and Tie were all famed in earlier histories.
translations.idiomatic: Pou's sons Yi, Ju, An, Wan, and Tie all won renown in earlier histories.

sentences.zh: 据子朗，字长度，位东阳太守。

translations.literal: Ju's son Lang, styled Changdu, held the post of Administrator of Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: Ju's son Lang, courtesy name Changdu, served as Administrator of Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 朗子重，字景重，位会稽王道子骠骑长史。

translations.literal: Lang's son Chong, styled Jingchong, held the post of Chief Clerk to the Cavalry General of Prince Daozi of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Lang's son Chong, courtesy name Jingchong, served as Chief Clerk to the Cavalry General of Prince Daozi of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 重生绚、瞻、晦、㬭爵、遯。

translations.literal: Chong had sons Xuan, Zhan, Hui, Shan Jue, and Dun.
translations.idiomatic: Chong fathered Xuan, Zhan, Hui, Shan Jue, and Dun.

sentences.zh: 绚位至宋武帝镇军长史，早卒。

translations.literal: Xuan rose to Chief Clerk of the Army of the General Who Guards the Army under Emperor Wu of Song, and died young.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan advanced to Chief Clerk of the Army under Emperor Wu's General Who Guards the Army, then died young.

sentences.zh: 晦初为孟昶建威府中兵参军。

translations.literal: Hui first served as Army Registrar in the Establishment of Might staff of Meng Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Hui began as Army Registrar on the staff of Meng Chang's Establishment of Might.

sentences.zh: 昶死，帝问刘穆之，"昶府谁堪入府？

translations.literal: When Chang died, the Emperor asked Liu Muzhi, "Who in Chang's office can enter the [Imperial] staff?"
translations.idiomatic: After Chang died, the Emperor asked Liu Muzhi, "Who from Chang's office is fit to join the imperial staff?"

sentences.zh: "穆之举晦，即命为太尉参军。

translations.literal: Muzhi recommended Hui, and he was immediately appointed Staff Officer to the Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Muzhi named Hui, who was at once made Staff Officer to the Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 武帝當訊獄，其旦，刑獄參軍有疾，以晦代之。

translations.literal: When the Emperor was to examine cases, that morning the Prison Affairs staff officer was ill, and Hui replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: One morning when the Emperor was to hear criminal cases, the prison-affairs staff officer fell ill and Hui took his place.

sentences.zh: 晦車中一覽訊牒，隨問，酬對無失。

translations.literal: In the carriage Hui read through the case dossier once; as questions followed, his answers missed nothing.
translations.idiomatic: In the carriage he skimmed the case file once; questioned point by point, he answered without a slip.

sentences.zh: 帝奇之，即日署刑獄賊曹。

translations.literal: The Emperor marveled at this and that same day appointed him to the Bureau of Prison Affairs and Bandit Suppression.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was astonished and that very day posted him to the Bureau of Prison Affairs and Bandit Suppression.

sentences.zh: 累遷太尉主簿。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Chief Clerk to the Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: He rose step by step to Chief Clerk to the Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 從征司馬休之，時徐逵之戰死，帝將自登岸，諸將諫不從。

translations.literal: Following the campaign against Sima Xiuzhi, Xu Daizhi died in battle; the Emperor was about to go ashore himself, and the generals remonstrated but he would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Following the campaign against Sima Xiuzhi, Xu Daizhi died in battle; the Emperor became about to go ashore himself, and the generals remonstrated but he would not listen.

sentences.zh: 晦抱持帝，帝曰：「我斬卿。

translations.literal: Hui held the Emperor fast; the Emperor said, "I will behead you."
translations.idiomatic: Hui seized and held the Emperor fast; the Emperor cried, "I'll have your head."

sentences.zh: 」晦曰：「天下可無晦，不可無公，晦死何有。

translations.literal: Hui said, "The realm can do without Hui; it cannot do without Your Majesty. What is Hui's death?"
translations.idiomatic: Hui replied, "The realm can spare Hui; it cannot spare Your Majesty. What is one man's death to that?"

sentences.zh: 」會胡藩登岸，賊退，乃止。

translations.literal: Just then Hu Fan went ashore, the bandits withdrew, and he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: At that moment Hu Fan gained the shore, the enemy fell back, and the Emperor relented.

sentences.zh: 晦美風姿，善言笑，眉目分明，鬢髮如墨。

translations.literal: Hui had fine bearing, was skilled in speech and laughter, with clear brows and eyes and temples and hair black as ink.
translations.idiomatic: Hui carried himself beautifully, spoke and laughed with grace, and had clear brows and eyes with temples and hair black as ink.

sentences.zh: 涉獵文義，博贍多通，時人以方楊德祖，微將不及。

translations.literal: He ranged through literary meaning, was broadly learned and masterful in many fields; contemporaries compared him to Yang Xiu, though slightly his inferior.
translations.idiomatic: He steeped himself in letters, was broadly learned and fluent in many subjects, and men of the day ranked him with Yang Xiu—though just shy of that mark.

sentences.zh: 晦聞猶以為恨。

translations.literal: When Hui heard this he still took it as a grievance.
translations.idiomatic: Hui heard this and still smarted at the slight.

sentences.zh: 帝深加愛賞，從征關、洛，內外要任悉委之。

translations.literal: The Emperor deeply favored and prized him; on the Guan and Luo campaigns, inside and outside, every key post was entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor deeply favored and prized him; on the Guan and Luo campaigns, inside and outside, every key post was entrusted to him.

sentences.zh: 帝于彭城大會，命紙筆賦詩，晦恐帝有失，起諫帝，即代作曰：「先蕩臨淄穢，卻清河洛塵，華陽有逸驥，桃林無伏輪。

translations.literal: At a great assembly at Pengcheng the Emperor ordered brush and paper for composing poems; Hui feared the Emperor might slip, rose and remonstrated with him, and at once composed in his stead: "First sweep Linzi's filth, then clear the dust of the Yellow and Luo; Huayang has a swift steed, Taolin no hidden wheel."
translations.idiomatic: At a great gathering in Pengcheng the Emperor called for brush and paper to compose verse; fearing a misstep, Hui rose to counsel him and on the spot wrote in his place: "First sweep Linzi's filth, then clear the Yellow and Luo of dust; Huayang holds a fleet courser, Taolin hides no wheel in ambush."

sentences.zh: 」於是群臣並作。

translations.literal: Thereupon all the ministers composed as well.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the ministers all composed poems too.

sentences.zh: 時謝混風華為江左第一，嘗與晦俱在武帝前，帝目之曰：「一時頓有兩玉人耳。」

translations.literal: At the time Xie Hun's elegance was first in the Jiangzuo region; once he and Hui were both before Emperor Wu, who looked at them and said, "For a moment there are two jade men."
translations.idiomatic: Then Xie Hun's elegance was first in the Jiangzuo region; once he and Hui were both before Emperor Wu, who looked at them and said, "For a moment there are two jade men."

sentences.zh: 劉穆之遣使陳事，晦往往異同，穆之怒曰：「公復有還時不？

translations.literal: When Liu Muzhi sent envoys to report affairs, Hui often differed with him; Muzhi angrily said, "Will the Duke ever return?"
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Muzhi's messengers reported on affairs, Hui often disagreed; Muzhi snapped, "Will the Duke ever come back?"

sentences.zh: 」及帝欲以晦為從事中郎，穆之堅執不與，故終穆之世不遷。

translations.literal: When the Emperor wished to make Hui Attendant Gentleman, Muzhi firmly refused to grant it, so through Muzhi's lifetime he was not transferred.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor wanted Hui as Attendant Gentleman, Muzhi held firm and denied the appointment, so Hui received no promotion while Muzhi lived.

sentences.zh: 及穆之喪問至，帝哭之甚慟，曰：「喪我賢友。

translations.literal: When word of Muzhi's death arrived, the Emperor wept with great grief and said, "I have lost a worthy friend."
translations.idiomatic: When news of Muzhi's death arrived, the Emperor wept bitterly and said, "I have lost a worthy friend."

sentences.zh: 」晦時正直，喜甚，自入合參審。

translations.literal: Hui was then on duty and was greatly pleased; he entered the inner office himself to verify.
translations.idiomatic: Hui became then on duty and was greatly pleased; he entered the inner office himself to verify.

sentences.zh: 其日教出，轉晦從事中郎。

translations.literal: That day an order issued transferring Hui to Attendant Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: That same day an edict came out promoting Hui to Attendant Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 宋台建，為右衛將軍，加侍中。

translations.literal: When the Song regime was established, he became General of the Right Guard and was given the post of Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When the Song regime was established, he became General of the Right Guard with the added title of Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 武帝聞咸陽淪沒，欲復北伐，晦諫以士馬疲怠，乃止。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu heard that Xianyang had fallen, he wished to campaign north again; Hui remonstrated that men and horses were weary, and he desisted.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu learned Xianyang had fallen he wanted another northern campaign; Hui urged that men and horses were exhausted, and the Emperor held back.

sentences.zh: 於是登城北望，慨然不悅，乃命群僚誦詩，晦詠王粲詩曰：「南登霸陵岸，回首望長安，悟彼下泉人，喟然傷心肝。

translations.literal: Thereupon he ascended the city wall and looked north, displeased and downcast, and ordered the officials to recite poetry; Hui chanted Wang Can's lines: "South I climb Baling's shore, turn back and gaze on Chang'an; I think on those beneath the hidden spring, and grief wrings my heart and liver."
translations.idiomatic: He mounted the city wall, looked north, and brooded in displeasure, then ordered the court to recite poetry; Hui intoned Wang Can's lines: "South I climb Baling's shore and turn back toward Chang'an; I think on souls beneath the hidden spring, and grief wrings my heart and liver."

sentences.zh: 」帝流涕不自勝。

translations.literal: The Emperor wept and could not master himself.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor wept and could not compose himself.

sentences.zh: 及帝受命，於石頭登壇，備法駕入宮，晦領遊軍為警。

translations.literal: When the Emperor received Heaven's mandate, at Shitou he ascended the altar; with full imperial equipage he entered the palace, and Hui led the mobile guard as escort.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor received Heaven's mandate he ascended the altar at Shitou; with full imperial equipage he entered the palace while Hui led the mobile guard on alert.

sentences.zh: 加中領軍，封武昌縣公。

translations.literal: He was made General of the Central Army and enfeoffed as Duke of Wuchang County.
translations.idiomatic: He became General of the Central Army and received enfeoffment as Duke of Wuchang County.

sentences.zh: 永初二年，坐行璽封鎮西司馬南郡太守王華，而誤封北海太守球，板免晦侍中。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongchu, for carrying the imperial seal to seal the appointment of Wang Hua as Administrator of Nan Commandery, Western Division Marshal, but mistakenly sealing Qiu as Administrator of Beihai, he was stripped of the post of Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongchu year two, charged with carrying the imperial seal to confirm Wang Hua as Western Division Marshal and Administrator of Nan Commandery but instead sealing Qiu as Administrator of Beihai, he was removed as Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 尋轉領軍將軍，加散騎常侍，依晉中軍羊祜故事，入直殿省，總統宿衛。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to General Who Leads the Army, with added title of Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry; following the precedent of Yang Hu, Central Army General under Jin, he entered duty in the palace offices and commanded the night guard.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, he became General Who Leads the Army, with added title of Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry; following the precedent of Yang Hu, Central Army General under Jin, he entered duty in the palace offices and commanded the night guard.

sentences.zh: 及帝不豫，給班劍二十人，與徐羨之、傅亮、檀道濟並侍醫藥。

translations.literal: When the Emperor fell ill, he was given twenty ceremonial swords and, with Xu Xianzhi, Fu Liang, and Tan Daoji, attended to his medical care.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor fell ill he received twenty ceremonial swords and, with Xu Xianzhi, Fu Liang, and Tan Daoji, attended the sickbed.

sentences.zh: 少帝即位，加中書令，與徐、傅輔政。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shao took the throne, Hui was made Director of the Secretariat and, with Xu and Fu, assisted in government.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shao ascended the throne, Hui was made Director of the Secretariat and governed alongside Xu and Fu.

sentences.zh: 及少帝廢，徐羨之以晦領護南蠻校尉、荊州刺史，加都督，欲令居外為援。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shao was deposed, Xu Xianzhi had Hui take the post of Colonel Protector of the Southern Barbarians and Governor of Jing Province, with added command authority, intending to place him outside as support.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Shao was deposed, Xu Xianzhi had Hui take Colonel Protector of the Southern Barbarians and Governor of Jing Province with full command, intending to keep him outside the capital as a reserve force.

sentences.zh: 慮文帝至，或別用人，故遽有此授。

translations.literal: Fearing that when Emperor Wen arrived someone else might be appointed, they hurriedly made this appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing that when Emperor Wen arrived another man might be placed in power, they rushed through this appointment.

sentences.zh: 精兵舊將，悉以配之。

translations.literal: Elite troops and veteran generals were all assigned to him.
translations.idiomatic: Crack troops and veteran generals were all assigned to his command.

sentences.zh: 文帝即位，晦慮不得去，甚憂惶。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen took the throne, Hui feared he would not be allowed to leave and was deeply anxious.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen took the throne, Hui feared he would not be permitted to leave the capital and was deeply anxious.

sentences.zh: 及發新亭，顧石頭城喜曰：「今得脫矣。

translations.literal: When he set out from Xinting he looked back at Shitou city and said with joy, "Now I have escaped."
translations.idiomatic: Setting out from Xinting he looked back at Shitou and said with relief, "At last I am free."

sentences.zh: 」進封建平郡公，固讓。

translations.literal: He was advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Jianping Commandery but firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised to Duke of Jianping Commandery but firmly declined the promotion.

sentences.zh: 又給鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: He was also given a set of ceremonial drums and horns.
translations.idiomatic: He was also granted a set of ceremonial drums and horns.

sentences.zh: 至江陵，深結侍中王華，冀以免禍。

translations.literal: At Jiangling he cultivated close ties with Palace Attendant Wang Hua, hoping thereby to escape disaster.
translations.idiomatic: At Jiangling he cultivated close ties with Palace Attendant Wang Hua, hoping to escape punishment.

sentences.zh: 二女當配彭城王義康、新野侯義賓。

translations.literal: Two daughters were to be matched to Prince Yikang of Pengcheng and Marquis Yibin of Xinye.
translations.idiomatic: Two daughters were betrothed to Prince Yikang of Pengcheng and Marquis Yibin of Xinye.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二年，遣妻及長子世休送女還都。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanjia he sent his wife and eldest son Shixiu to escort the daughters back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia year two he sent his wife and eldest son Shixiu to escort the daughters back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 先是，景平中，魏師攻取河南，至是欲誅羨之等並討晦，聲言北行，又言拜京陵，裝舟艦。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the Jingping era, Wei forces had seized Henan; now the court intended to execute Xianzhi and the others and punish Hui, publicly announcing a northern march while also saying they would worship at the imperial tombs near the capital and fitting out ships.
translations.idiomatic: Before this, in the Jingping era, Wei forces had seized Henan; now the court intended to execute Xianzhi and the others and punish Hui, publicly announcing a northern march while also saying they would worship at the imperial tombs near the capital and fitting out ships.

sentences.zh: 傅亮與晦書，言：「薄伐河朔，事猶未已，朝野之慮，憂懼者多」。

translations.literal: Fu Liang wrote to Hui saying, "The slight campaign on the north bank of the Yellow River is not yet finished; court and countryside alike are full of worry and fear."
translations.idiomatic: Fu Liang wrote Hui: "The limited campaign north of the Yellow River is not yet finished; court and countryside alike seethe with worry and fear."

sentences.zh: 又言：「當遣外監萬幼宗往「。

translations.literal: He also said, "The outer supervisor Wan Youzong is to be sent."
translations.idiomatic: He added, "The outer supervisor Wan Youzong is to be dispatched."

sentences.zh: 時朝廷處分異常，其謀頗泄。

translations.literal: At the time the court's measures were unusual, and the plot leaked in large part.
translations.idiomatic: The court's movements were abnormal, and much of the plot leaked out.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，晦弟黃門侍郎嚼馳使告晦，晦猶謂不然，呼諮議參軍何承天示以亮書曰：「計幼宗一二日必至，傅公慮我好事，故先遣此書。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year, Hui's younger brother, Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Jiao, sent a fast courier to warn Hui; Hui still thought it untrue, summoned Staff Officer He Chengtian, showed him Liang's letter and said, "Youzong should arrive in a day or two; Master Fu feared I would meddle and so sent this letter first."
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year three, Hui's brother Jiao, Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, sent a fast courier to warn him; Hui still disbelieved, called in Staff Officer He Chengtian, showed him Liang's letter and said, "Youzong ought to arrive within a day or two; Master Fu feared I would stir trouble and so sent this letter ahead."

sentences.zh: 」承天曰：「外間所聞，咸謂西討已定，幼宗豈有上理？

translations.literal: Chengtian said, "What people outside hear is that the western punitive campaign is already settled; how could Youzong still be coming?"
translations.idiomatic: Chengtian said, "Outside rumor has it the western punitive expedition is already decided; why would Youzong still be on his way?"

sentences.zh: 」晦尚謂虛，使承天豫立答詔啟草，北行宜須明年。

translations.literal: Hui still thought it empty; he had Chengtian prepare a draft reply to the edict in advance, saying the northern march should wait until next year.
translations.idiomatic: Hui still treated it as empty talk and had Chengtian draft a reply in advance, arguing the northern march should wait until the next year.

sentences.zh: 江夏內史程道慧得尋陽人書，言其事已審，使示晦。

translations.literal: Interior Administrator of Jiangxia Cheng Daohui received a letter from a man of Xunyang saying the matter was confirmed, and had it shown to Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangxia Interior Administrator Cheng Daohui received a letter from a man of Xunyang saying the matter was settled and showed it to Hui.

sentences.zh: 晦問計於承天，對曰：「蒙將軍殊顧，常思報德，事變至矣，何敢隱情。

translations.literal: Hui asked Chengtian's counsel; he answered, "I have received the General's extraordinary favor and always wished to repay it; the crisis has arrived—how dare I hide the truth?"
translations.idiomatic: Hui asked Chengtian's advice; he answered, "Your Grace has shown me extraordinary favor and I have long wished to repay it; the crisis is here—how could I conceal what I know?"

sentences.zh: 然明日戒嚴，動用軍法，區區所懷，懼不得盡。

translations.literal: Yet tomorrow there will be martial law and military justice; what little I feel in my heart, I fear I cannot fully speak.
translations.idiomatic: Yet tomorrow martial law will be declared and military justice enforced; what I feel in my heart, I fear I cannot say it all.

sentences.zh: 」晦懼曰：「卿豈欲我自裁哉？

translations.literal: Hui said in fear, "Do you want me to kill myself?"
translations.idiomatic: Hui said in alarm, "Do you mean I should take my own life?"

sentences.zh: 」承天曰：「尚未至此，其在境外。

translations.literal: Chengtian said, "It has not come to that; the way lies outside the borders."
translations.idiomatic: Chengtian said, "Not yet; the path lies beyond the frontier."

sentences.zh: 」晦曰：「荊州用武之地，兵糧易給。

translations.literal: Hui said, "Jing Province is a land of military advantage; arms and grain are easy to supply."
translations.idiomatic: Hui said, "Jing Province is a natural battlefield; arms and grain are easy to gather."

sentences.zh: 聊且決戰，走復何晚。

translations.literal: For now let us fight it out; flight would come none too late.
translations.idiomatic: Let us fight it out for now; flight would not come too late.

sentences.zh: 吾不愛死，負先帝之顧，如何？

translations.literal: I do not grudge death, but how can I betray the late Emperor's trust?
translations.idiomatic: I do not begrudge death—but how can I betray the late Emperor's trust?

sentences.zh: 」又謂承天曰：「幼宗尚未至，若後二三日無消息，便是不復來邪？

translations.literal: He also said to Chengtian, "Youzong has not yet arrived; if in two or three days there is no word, then he is not coming at all, is he?"
translations.idiomatic: He likewise said to Chengtian, "Youzong has not yet arrived; if in two or three days there is no word, then he is not coming at all, is he?"

sentences.zh: 」承天曰：「程說其事已判，豈容復疑。

translations.literal: Chengtian said, "Cheng says the matter is already decided; how can there still be doubt?"
translations.idiomatic: Chengtian said, "Cheng says the matter is already settled; how can doubt remain?"

sentences.zh: 」晦欲焚南蠻兵籍，率見力決戰。

translations.literal: Hui wished to burn the Southern Barbarian muster rolls and lead the available forces to a decisive battle.
translations.idiomatic: Hui meant to burn the Southern Barbarian muster rolls and lead every man he had into decisive battle.

sentences.zh: 土人多勸發兵。

translations.literal: Local men mostly urged raising troops.
translations.idiomatic: Local men mostly urged him to raise troops.

sentences.zh: 晦問諸將：「戰士三千足守城乎？

translations.literal: Hui asked the generals, "Are three thousand fighting men enough to hold the city?"
translations.idiomatic: Hui asked his generals, "Are three thousand fighting men enough to hold the city?"

sentences.zh: 」南蠻司馬周超曰：「非徒守城；

translations.literal: Southern Barbarians Major Zhou Chao said, "Not only to hold the city;"
translations.idiomatic: Southern Barbarians Major Zhou Chao said, "Not merely to hold the city—"

sentences.zh: 若有外寇，亦可立勳。

translations.literal: if there were an outside enemy, one could also win merit.
translations.idiomatic: given an outside foe, one could also win glory in battle.

sentences.zh: 」司馬庾登之請解司馬、南郡以授之，晦即命超為司馬，轉登之為長史。

translations.literal: Major Yu Dengzhi asked to be relieved of his major's post and Nan Commandery and have it given to Chao; Hui at once made Chao major and transferred Dengzhi to Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Major Yu Dengzhi asked to surrender his major's post and Nan Commandery to Chao; Hui at once made Chao major and transferred Dengzhi to Chief Clerk.

sentences.zh: 文帝誅羨之等及晦子世休，收嚼、嚼子世平、兄子紹等。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen executed Xianzhi and the others and Hui's son Shixiu, he arrested Jiao, Jiao's son Shiping, and his elder brother's son Shao.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen executed Xianzhi and the others and Hui's son Shixiu, he also arrested Jiao, Jiao's son Shiping, and Hui's nephew Shao.

sentences.zh: 晦知訖，先舉羨之、亮哀，次發子弟凶問。

translations.literal: When Hui learned of it, he first raised mourning for Xianzhi and Liang, then announced the grim news about his kinsmen.
translations.idiomatic: When Hui learned of it he first raised mourning for Xianzhi and Liang, then announced the grim news about his kinsmen.

sentences.zh: 既而自出射堂，集得精兵三萬人，乃奉表，言：「臣等若志欲專權，不顧國典，便當輔翼幼主，孤背天日，豈得沿流二千，虛館三月，奉迎鑾駕，以遵下武。

translations.literal: Then he himself came out to the archery hall, mustered thirty thousand elite troops, and submitted a memorial saying, "If we ministers had wished to monopolize power and heedless of the state's laws, we would have supported the young lord and turned our backs on Heaven—how could we have drifted two thousand li downstream, lodged idle for three months, and welcomed the imperial carriage to follow the example of King Wu?"
translations.idiomatic: Then he came out to the archery hall, mustered thirty thousand elite troops, and submitted a memorial: "Had we wished to monopolize power regardless of the state's laws, we would have propped up the young emperor and turned our backs on Heaven—how could we have drifted two thousand li downstream, lodged idle for three months, and welcomed the imperial carriage in the manner of King Wu?"

sentences.zh: 故廬陵王于營陽之世，屢彼猜嫌，積怨犯上，自貽非命。

translations.literal: Formerly Prince Luling in Emperor Yingyang's time was repeatedly suspected and resented; he piled up grievances and offended his superiors, bringing ruin on himself.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Prince Luling in Emperor Yingyang's time became repeatedly suspected and resented; he piled up grievances and offended his superiors, bringing ruin on himself.

sentences.zh: 不有所廢，將何以興，耿弇不以賊遺君父，臣亦何負于宋室邪。

translations.literal: If the unworthy is not removed, how can the worthy be raised? Geng Yan did not leave the enemy for lord and father; how have I wronged the house of Song?
translations.idiomatic: If the unworthy is not removed, how can the worthy be raised? Geng Yan did not leave the enemy for lord and father—how have I wronged the house of Song?

sentences.zh: 」又言：「羨之、亮無罪見誅，王弘兄弟輕躁昧進，王華猜忌忍害」。

translations.literal: He also said, "Xianzhi and Liang were guiltless yet executed; Wang Hong and his brothers were rash and blindly ambitious; Wang Hua was suspicious and cruel."
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote, "Xianzhi and Liang were guiltless yet executed; Wang Hong and his brothers were rash and blindly ambitious; Wang Hua was suspicious and cruel."

sentences.zh: 帝時已戒嚴，尚書符荊州暴其罪狀。

translations.literal: The Emperor had already declared martial law; the Secretariat issued orders to Jing Province proclaiming their crimes.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had already declared martial law; the Secretariat issued orders to Jing Province proclaiming their crimes.

sentences.zh: 晦率眾二萬發自江陵，舟艦列自江津至於破塚，旗旌相照。

translations.literal: Hui led twenty thousand men setting out from Jiangling; warships lined the route from Jiangjin to Pojia, banners and flags gleaming one upon another.
translations.idiomatic: Hui led twenty thousand men out from Jiangling; warships lined the route from Jiangjin to Pojia, banners and flags shining one upon another.

sentences.zh: 歎曰：「恨不得以此為勤王之師。

translations.literal: He sighed and said, "Ah, that this could not be an army to rescue the throne."
translations.idiomatic: He sighed and said, "Would that this force could have been an army to rescue the throne."

sentences.zh: 」移檄建鄴，言王弘、曇首、王華等罪。

translations.literal: He issued a proclamation to Jiankang denouncing the crimes of Wang Hong, Tan Shou, Wang Hua, and others.
translations.idiomatic: He issued a proclamation to Jiankang denouncing Wang Hong, Tan Shou, Wang Hua, and the rest.

sentences.zh: 又上表陳情。

translations.literal: He also submitted a memorial stating his grievance.
translations.idiomatic: He also submitted a memorial stating his case.

sentences.zh: 初，晦與徐、傅謀為自全計：晦據上流，檀鎮廣陵，各有強兵，足制朝廷；

translations.literal: Earlier, Hui with Xu and Fu had plotted for self-preservation: Hui would hold the upper reaches, Tan would garrison Guangling, each with strong forces enough to control the court;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Hui, Xu, and Fu had plotted for self-preservation: Hui would hold the upper Yangtze, Tan would garrison Guangling, each with forces strong enough to control the court;

sentences.zh: 羨之、亮于中知權，可得持久。

translations.literal: Xianzhi and Liang at the center would wield power and could endure.
translations.idiomatic: while Xianzhi and Liang at the center wielded power and could hold out.

sentences.zh: 及帝將行，召檀道濟委之以眾。

translations.literal: When the Emperor was about to march, he summoned Tan Daoji and entrusted the army to him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor prepared to march, he summoned Tan Daoji and entrusted the army to him.

sentences.zh: 晦始謂道濟不全，及聞其來，大眾皆潰。

translations.literal: Hui had first thought Daoji would not come in full; when he heard he was coming, the great host mostly scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Hui had first thought Daoji would not come in full; when he heard he became coming, the great host mostly scattered.

sentences.zh: 晦得小船還江陵。

translations.literal: Hui got a small boat and returned to Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Hui took a small boat and fled back to Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 初，雍州刺史劉粹遣弟竟陵太守道濟與台軍主沈敞之襲江陵，至沙橋，周超大破之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Governor of Yong Province Liu Cui had sent his younger brother, Administrator of Jingling Liu Daoji, with the capital army commander Shen Changzhi to strike Jiangling; at Shaqiao, Zhou Chao routed them completely.
translations.idiomatic: Before this, Governor of Yong Province Liu Cui had sent his younger brother, Administrator of Jingling Liu Daoji, with the capital army commander Shen Changzhi to strike Jiangling; at Shaqiao, Zhou Chao routed them completely.

sentences.zh: 俄而晦至江陵，無他處分，唯愧謝周超而已。

translations.literal: Soon Hui reached Jiangling and made no other disposition; he only apologized to Zhou Chao in shame.
translations.idiomatic: When Hui reached Jiangling he made no other disposition; he only apologized to Zhou Chao in shame.

sentences.zh: 超其夜詣到彥之降，晦乃攜弟遯兄子世基等七騎北走。

translations.literal: That night Chao went to Dao Yanzhi to surrender; Hui then fled north with seven riders—his brother Dun, his elder brother's son Shiji, and others.
translations.idiomatic: That night Chao went to Dao Yanzhi and surrendered; Hui then fled north with seven riders—his brother Dun, his nephew Shiji, and others.

sentences.zh: 遯肥不能騎馬，晦每待不得速。

translations.literal: Dun was too fat to ride a horse; Hui always had to wait and could not go fast.
translations.idiomatic: Dun was too stout to ride; Hui always had to wait for him and could not flee quickly.

sentences.zh: 至安陸延頭，晦故吏戍主光順之檻送建鄴。

translations.literal: At Yantou in Anlu, Guang Shunzhi, a former subordinate and garrison commander, put him in a cage and sent him to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: At Yantou in Anlu, Guang Shunzhi, a former subordinate and garrison commander, caged him and sent him to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 于路作悲人道以自哀。

translations.literal: On the road he composed "Lament for a Fallen Man" to mourn himself.
translations.idiomatic: On the road he composed "Lament for a Fallen Man" to mourn his own fall.

sentences.zh: 周超既降，到彥之以參府事。

translations.literal: After Zhou Chao surrendered, Dao Yanzhi made him a staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhou Chao surrendered, Dao Yanzhi took him onto his staff.

sentences.zh: 劉粹遣告彥之，沙橋之事，敗由周超。

translations.literal: Liu Cui sent word to Yanzhi that the defeat at Shaqiao was Zhou Chao's fault.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cui sent word to Yanzhi that the defeat at Shaqiao was Zhou Chao's doing.

sentences.zh: 彥之乃執與晦等並伏誅。

translations.literal: Yanzhi then seized him and he was executed together with Hui and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhi then seized him, and he was executed together with Hui and the others.

sentences.zh: 世基，絢之子也。

translations.literal: Shiji was Xuan's son.
translations.idiomatic: Shiji was the son of Xuan.

sentences.zh: 有才氣，臨死為連句詩曰：「偉哉橫海鱗，壯矣垂天翼，一旦失風水，翻為螻蟻食。

translations.literal: Talented and spirited, facing death he composed linked-verse poetry: "Vast the sea-spanning fish, mighty the sky-hanging wing; once wind and water are lost, it becomes food for ants."
translations.idiomatic: Talented and spirited, facing death he composed linked verse: "Vast the sea-spanning fish, mighty the sky-hanging wing; once wind and water fail, it becomes food for ants."

sentences.zh: 」晦續之曰：「功遂侔昔人，保退無智力。

translations.literal: Hui continued: "Merit done, I match the men of old; safe withdrawal—no wisdom or strength."
translations.idiomatic: Hui continued: "Merit achieved, I match the men of old; safe withdrawal—no wisdom, no strength."

sentences.zh: 既涉太行險，斯路信難陟。

translations.literal: Having crossed the peril of the Taihang, this road is truly hard to climb.
translations.idiomatic: Once past the peril of the Taihang, this road is truly hard to climb.

sentences.zh: 」晦女為彭城王義康妃，聰明有才貌，被髮徒跣與晦訣曰：「阿父，大丈夫當橫屍戰場，奈何狼藉都市。

translations.literal: Hui's daughter was consort to Prince Yikang of Pengcheng—intelligent, talented, and beautiful; with hair loose and barefoot she took leave of Hui and said, "Father, a great man should lie dead on the battlefield—how can he be strewn in disgrace through the capital?"
translations.idiomatic: Hui's daughter became consort to Prince Yikang of Pengcheng—intelligent, talented, and beautiful; with hair loose and barefoot she took leave of Hui and said, "Father, a great man should lie dead on the battlefield—how can he be strewn in disgrace through the capital?"

sentences.zh: 」言訖叫絕，行人為之落淚。

translations.literal: When she finished she shrieked and fainted; passersby wept for her.
translations.idiomatic: When she finished she shrieked and collapsed; passersby wept at the sight.

sentences.zh: 晦死時年三十七。

translations.literal: When Hui died he was thirty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was thirty-seven when he died.

sentences.zh: 庾登之、殷道鸞、何承天自晦下並見原。

translations.literal: Yu Dengzhi, Yin Daoluan, and He Chengtian, from the time of Hui's fall, were all pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Dengzhi, Yin Daoluan, and He Chengtian were all pardoned after Hui's fall.

sentences.zh: 次兄 瞻

translations.literal: Second elder brother Zhan
translations.idiomatic: The second elder brother, Zhan

sentences.zh: 瞻字宣遠，一曰名簷字通遠，晦次兄也。

translations.literal: Zhan, styled Xuanyuan—one account gives his name as Yan and style Tongyuan—was Hui's next elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan, courtesy name Xuanyuan—one account gives his name as Yan and style Tongyuan—was Hui's next elder brother.

sentences.zh: 六歲能屬文，為紫石英贊、果然詩，為當時才士歎異。

translations.literal: At six he could compose prose; he wrote "Ode to Amethyst Quartz" and "Poem on the Guoran Bird," and the talented men of the day marveled.
translations.idiomatic: At six he could compose prose; his "Ode to Amethyst Quartz" and "Poem on the Guoran Bird" astonished the talented men of the day.

sentences.zh: 與從叔混、族弟靈運俱有盛名。

translations.literal: With his father's younger cousin Hun and his clansman younger brother Lingyun he all had great fame.
translations.idiomatic: He shared great fame with his father's younger cousin Hun and his clansman Lingyun.

sentences.zh: 嘗作喜霽詩，靈運寫之，混詠之。

translations.literal: Once he composed a poem on fine clear weather; Lingyun wrote it out and Hun chanted it.
translations.idiomatic: Once he wrote a poem on fine clear weather; Lingyun copied it out and Hun recited it.

sentences.zh: 王弘在坐，以為三絕。

translations.literal: Wang Hong was present and deemed it a triple perfection.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hong was present and called it a triple perfection.

sentences.zh: 瞻幼孤，叔母劉撫養有恩，兄弟事之同於至親。

translations.literal: Zhan was orphaned young; his aunt Liu raised him with kindness, and the brothers served her as they would their closest kin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan became orphaned young; his aunt Liu raised him with kindness, and the brothers served her as they would their closest kin.

sentences.zh: 劉弟柳為吳郡，將姊俱行，瞻不能違遠，自楚台秘書郎解職隨從，故為柳建威長史。

translations.literal: Liu's younger brother Liu was Administrator of Wu Commandery and was taking his sister along; Zhan could not bear to be far away, resigned his post as Secretary of the Chu's Terrace and followed, and so became Chief Clerk on Liu's Establishment of Might staff.
translations.idiomatic: Liu's younger brother Liu became Administrator of Wu Commandery and was taking his sister along; Zhan could not bear to be far away, resigned his post as Secretary of the Chu's Terrace and followed, and so became Chief Clerk on Liu's Establishment of Might staff.

sentences.zh: 後為宋武帝相國從事中郎。

translations.literal: Later he became Attendant Gentleman on the staff of Emperor Wu of Song as Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served as Attendant Gentleman on Emperor Wu's chancellery staff.

sentences.zh: 晦時為宋台右衛，權遇已重，于彭城還都迎家，賓客輻湊。

translations.literal: When Hui was General of the Right Guard of the Song regime his power and favor were already heavy; returning from Pengcheng to the capital to welcome his family, guests thronged.
translations.idiomatic: When Hui became General of the Right Guard of the Song regime his power and favor were already heavy; returning from Pengcheng to the capital to welcome his family, guests thronged.

sentences.zh: 時瞻在家，驚駭謂晦曰：「吾家以素退為業，汝遂勢傾朝野，此豈門戶福邪。

translations.literal: Zhan was then at home and said in alarm to Hui, "Our house has always taken modest retreat as its business; you have now tilted power across court and countryside—is this a blessing to our gate?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhan became then at home and said in alarm to Hui, "Our house has always taken modest retreat as its business; you have now tilted power across court and countryside—is this a blessing to our gate?"

sentences.zh: 」乃籬隔門庭，曰：「吾不忍見此。

translations.literal: He then fenced off the courtyard with a hedge and said, "I cannot bear to see this."
translations.idiomatic: He fenced off the courtyard with a hedge and said, "I cannot bear to see this."

sentences.zh: 」後因宴集，靈運問晦：「潘、陸與賈充優劣。

translations.literal: Later at a banquet Lingyun asked Hui, "Which were superior, Pan and Lu or Jia Chong?"
translations.idiomatic: Later at a banquet Lingyun asked Hui, "Which were superior—Pan and Lu, or Jia Chong?"

sentences.zh: 」晦曰：「安仁諂於權門，士衡邀競無已，並不能保身，自求多福。

translations.literal: Hui said, "Anren flattered the powerful; Shiheng ceaselessly sought rivalry—neither could preserve himself or seek more blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Hui said, "Anren flattered the powerful; Shiheng ceaselessly sought rivalry—neither could preserve himself or secure his own good fortune.

sentences.zh: 公閭勳名佐世，不得為並。

translations.literal: Gonglu's merit and fame assisted his age; he cannot be ranked with them.
translations.idiomatic: Gonglu's merit and fame served his age; he cannot be ranked with them."

sentences.zh: 」靈運曰：「安仁、士衡才為一時之冠，方之公閭，本自遼絕。

translations.literal: Lingyun said, "Anren and Shiheng's talent was the crown of their age; compared with Gonglu, they were utterly beyond reach from the start."
translations.idiomatic: Lingyun said, "Anren and Shiheng's talent became the crown of their age; compared with Gonglu, they were utterly beyond reach from the start."

sentences.zh: 」瞻斂容曰：「若處貴而能遺權，斯則是非不得而生，傾危無因而至。

translations.literal: Zhan composed his face and said, "If one in high position can relinquish power, then right and wrong cannot arise and peril cannot come unbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan composed his face and said, "If one in high place can relinquish power, right and wrong cannot arise and peril cannot come unbidden.

sentences.zh: 君子以明哲保身，其在此乎。

translations.literal: The noble man preserves himself through clear wisdom—is it not here?"
translations.idiomatic: A noble man preserves himself through clear wisdom—is it not here?"

sentences.zh: 」常以裁止晦如此。

translations.literal: He often checked Hui in this way.
translations.idiomatic: This man often checked Hui in this way.

sentences.zh: 及還彭城，言于武帝曰：「臣本素士，父祖位不過二千石。

translations.literal: When he returned to Pengcheng he said to Emperor Wu, "I was originally a plain scholar; my father and grandfather's posts did not exceed two-thousand-shi rank.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned to Pengcheng he said to Emperor Wu, "I became originally a plain scholar; my father and grandfather's posts did not exceed two-thousand-shi rank.

sentences.zh: 弟年始三十，志用凡近，位任顯密，福過災生，特乞降黜，以保衰門。

translations.literal: My younger brother is only thirty; his aims and capacity are ordinary, yet his post is conspicuous and secret—blessing passed, disaster born; I specially beg demotion to preserve our declining house."
translations.idiomatic: My younger brother is only thirty; his aims and capacity are ordinary, yet his post is conspicuous and secret—blessing has outrun merit and disaster follows; I beg demotion to preserve our declining house."

sentences.zh: 」前後屢陳。

translations.literal: He submitted this repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: This man submitted this repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 帝欲以瞻為吳興郡，又自陳請，乃為豫章太守。

translations.literal: The Emperor wished to make Zhan Administrator of Wuxing; he petitioned again himself and was made Administrator of Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor wished to make Zhan Administrator of Wuxing; Zhan petitioned again and was given Yuzhang instead.

sentences.zh: 晦或以朝廷密事語瞻，瞻輒向親舊說以為戲笑，以絕其言。

translations.literal: When Hui sometimes told Zhan court secrets, Zhan would tell kin and friends as jest to cut off such talk.
translations.idiomatic: When Hui sometimes confided court secrets, Zhan would repeat them to kin and friends as a jest, to choke off such talk.

sentences.zh: 晦遂建佐命功，瞻愈憂懼。

translations.literal: Hui then achieved merit in founding the dynasty; Zhan grew ever more fearful.
translations.idiomatic: When Hui earned merit in founding the dynasty, Zhan grew ever more fearful.

sentences.zh: 永初二年，在郡遇疾不療，幸於不永。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongchu, while in his commandery he fell ill and did not recover; he counted himself fortunate not to live long.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongchu year two, ill in his commandery and failing to recover, he counted himself fortunate not to live long.

sentences.zh: 晦聞疾奔波，瞻見之曰：「汝為國大臣，又總戎重，萬里遠出，必生疑謗。

translations.literal: When Hui heard he rushed there; Zhan saw him and said, "You are a great minister of the state and also hold overall military weight; to travel ten thousand li is sure to breed suspicion and slander."
translations.idiomatic: When Hui heard he rushed there; Zhan saw him and said, "You are a great minister of the state and hold overall military command; to travel ten thousand li is sure to breed suspicion and slander."

sentences.zh: 」時果有詐告晦反者。

translations.literal: At the time there was indeed a false report that Hui had rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Then there was indeed a false report that Hui had rebelled.

sentences.zh: 瞻疾篤還都，帝以晦禁旅，不得出宿，使瞻居於晉南郡公主婿羊賁故第，在領軍府東門。

translations.literal: Zhan's illness grew grave and he returned to the capital; because Hui held the palace guard and could not lodge outside, the Emperor had Zhan stay at the former residence of Yang Ben, son-in-law of the Jin Princess of Nan Commandery, east of the General Who Leads the Army's office.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan's illness grew grave and he returned to the capital; because Hui held the palace guard and could not lodge outside, the emperor had Zhan stay at the former residence of Yang Ben, son-in-law of the Jin Princess of Nan Commandery, east of the General Who Leads the Army's office.

sentences.zh: 瞻曰：「吾有先人弊廬，何為於此？

translations.literal: Zhan said, "I have my forebears' humble dwelling—why here?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhan said: "I have my forebears' humble dwelling—why here?"

sentences.zh: 」臨終遺晦書曰：「吾得歸骨山足，亦何所多恨。

translations.literal: On his deathbed he left Hui a letter saying, "I can return my bones to the mountain's foot—what more is there to regret?"
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed he left Hui a letter: "I can return my bones to the mountain's foot—what more is there to regret?"

sentences.zh: 弟思自勉，為國為家。

translations.literal: Younger brother, strive on your own—for the state and for the family.
translations.idiomatic: Brother, strive on your own—for the state and for the family.

sentences.zh: 」卒時年三十五。

translations.literal: When he died he was thirty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He was thirty-five when he died.

sentences.zh: 瞻文章之美，與從叔混、族弟靈運相抗。

translations.literal: Zhan's literary beauty matched his father's younger cousin Hun and his clansman Lingyun.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan's literary gifts matched his father's younger cousin Hun and his clansman Lingyun.

sentences.zh: 靈運父瑍無才能，為秘書郎早卒，而靈運好臧否人物。

translations.literal: Lingyun's father Min had no talent; he was Secretary Lang and died young, yet Lingyun loved to judge people's merits and faults.
translations.idiomatic: Lingyun's father Min had no talent; he became Secretary Lang and died young, yet Lingyun loved to judge people's merits and faults.

sentences.zh: 混患之，欲加裁折，未有其方。

translations.literal: Hun was troubled by this and wished to check him but had no means.
translations.idiomatic: Hun was troubled and wished to check him but had no means.

sentences.zh: 謂瞻曰：「非汝莫能。

translations.literal: He said to Zhan, "No one but you can do it."
translations.idiomatic: He told Zhan, "No one but you can do it."

sentences.zh: 」乃與晦、曜、弘微等共遊戲，使瞻與靈運共車。

translations.literal: He then went out with Hui, Yao, Hongwei, and others to amuse themselves and had Zhan ride in the same carriage as Lingyun.
translations.idiomatic: He then went out with Hui, Yao, Hongwei, and others for amusement and had Zhan ride in the same carriage as Lingyun.

sentences.zh: 靈運登車便商較人物，瞻謂曰：「秘書早亡，談者亦互有同異。

translations.literal: Lingyun boarded and at once began comparing people's merits; Zhan said to him, "Secretary Lang died young, and those who speak of him also differ among themselves."
translations.idiomatic: Lingyun boarded and at once began ranking people; Zhan said, "Secretary Lang died young, and those who speak of him differ among themselves."

sentences.zh: 」靈運默然，言論自此衰止。

translations.literal: Lingyun fell silent, and from then on such talk declined and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Lingyun fell silent, and from then on such talk dwindled and stopped.

sentences.zh: 弟嚼字宣鏡，年數歲，所生母郭氏疾，嚼晨昏溫凊，勤容戚顏，未嘗暫改。

translations.literal: Younger brother Jiao, styled Xuanjing, was a few years old when his birth-mother Lady Guo fell ill; morning and evening he attended her with warm care, his bearing always sorrowful, never briefly changing.
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother Jiao, courtesy name Xuanjing, was a few years old when his birth-mother Lady Guo fell ill; morning and evening he attended her with warm care, his bearing always sorrowful, never briefly changing.

sentences.zh: 恐僕役營疾懈倦，躬自執勞，母為疾畏驚，而微踐過甚，一家尊卑感嚼至性，咸納屨行、屏氣語，如此者十餘年。

translations.literal: Fearing the servants tending the illness might slacken, he personally took the labor; his mother, startled by the illness, needed quiet, and he stepped too lightly—everyone high and low in the house was moved by Jiao's utmost filial nature and all removed their shoes and lowered their voices when speaking, for more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the servants tending the illness might slacken, he personally took the labor; his mother, startled by the illness, needed quiet, and he stepped too lightly—everyone high and low in the house became moved by Jiao's utmost filial nature and all removed their shoes and lowered their voices when speaking, for more than ten years.

sentences.zh: 位黃門侍郎，從坐伏誅。

translations.literal: He held the post of Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and was executed as an associate.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and was executed as an associate in the crime.

sentences.zh: 從叔 澹

translations.literal: Father's younger cousin Dan
translations.idiomatic: The father's younger cousin, Dan

sentences.zh: 澹字景恒，晦從叔也。

translations.literal: Dan, styled Jingheng, was Hui's father's younger cousin.
translations.idiomatic: Dan, courtesy name Jingheng, was Hui's father's younger cousin.

sentences.zh: 祖安，晉太傅。

translations.literal: Grandfather An was Grand Tutor under Jin.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather An was Grand Tutor under Jin.

sentences.zh: 父瑤，琅邪王友。

translations.literal: Father Yao was Friend to the Prince of Langye.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yao was Friend to the Prince of Langye.

sentences.zh: 澹任達仗氣，不營當世，與順陽范泰為雲霞之交。

translations.literal: Dan was free and bold, trusting in his spirit, did not pursue worldly success, and with Shunyang's Fan Tai had a friendship lofty as clouds and mist.
translations.idiomatic: Dan was free and bold, trusting in his spirit, cared nothing for worldly success, and with Fan Tai of Shunyang kept a friendship lofty as clouds and mist.

sentences.zh: 歷位尚書。

translations.literal: He held posts up to Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 宋武帝將受禪，有司議使侍中劉叡進璽，帝曰：「此選當須人望。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Song was about to receive the abdication, the relevant offices debated having Attendant Gentleman Liu Rui present the seal; the Emperor said, "This choice must be a man of public esteem."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Song became about to receive the abdication, the relevant offices debated having Attendant Gentleman Liu Rui present the seal; the Emperor said, "This choice must be a man of public esteem."

sentences.zh: 」乃使澹攝。

translations.literal: He then had Dan act in the role.
translations.idiomatic: Then he had Dan act in the role.

sentences.zh: 澹嘗侍帝宴，酣飲大言無所屈，鄭鮮之欲按之，帝以為澹方外士，不宜規矩繩之；

translations.literal: Dan once attended the Emperor at a banquet, drank deeply and spoke boldly without bending; Zheng Xianzhi wished to impeach him, but the Emperor thought Dan was a man beyond the world and should not be bound by square rules;
translations.idiomatic: Dan once attended the Emperor at a banquet, drank deeply and spoke boldly without bending; Zheng Xianzhi wished to impeach him, but the Emperor thought Dan a man beyond the world and not to be bound by square rules;

sentences.zh: 然意不說，不以任寄。

translations.literal: yet he was displeased at heart and did not entrust him with office.
translations.idiomatic: yet he became displeased at heart and did not entrust him with office.

sentences.zh: 後復侍飲，醉謂帝曰：「陛下用群臣，但須委屈順者乃見貴，汲黯之徒無用也。

translations.literal: Later attending again while drunk he said to the Emperor, "Your Majesty uses your ministers—you need only those who yield and comply to be honored; men like Ji An are useless."
translations.idiomatic: Later, drunk at another audience, he told the Emperor, "Your Majesty uses ministers—you need only those who yield and comply to be honored; men like Ji An are useless."

sentences.zh: 」帝大笑。

translations.literal: The Emperor laughed heartily.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor laughed heartily.

sentences.zh: 景平中，累遷光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the Jingping era he was promoted in succession to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jingping era he rose step by step to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 從子晦為荊州，將之鎮，詣澹別。

translations.literal: When his nephew Hui was Governor of Jing Province and was going to his post, he came to Dan to take leave.
translations.idiomatic: When his nephew Hui was Governor of Jing Province and was leaving for his post, he came to Dan to take leave.

sentences.zh: 晦色自矜，澹問晦年，答曰三十五。

translations.literal: Hui's face was self-satisfied; Dan asked Hui's age and he answered thirty-five.
translations.idiomatic: Hui looked self-satisfied; Dan asked his age and he answered thirty-five.

sentences.zh: 澹笑曰：「昔荀中郎年二十九為北府都督，卿比之已為老矣。

translations.literal: Dan laughed and said, "In old days Xun Zhonglang at twenty-nine was Northern Headquarters Commander—you compared with him are already old."
translations.idiomatic: Dan laughed and said, "In old days Xun Zhonglang at twenty-nine was Northern Headquarters Commander—you, compared with him, are already old."

sentences.zh: 」晦色甚愧。

translations.literal: Hui's face was deeply ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Hui flushed with shame.

sentences.zh: 元嘉中，位侍中、特進、金紫光祿大夫，卒。

translations.literal: In the Yuanjia era he held Palace Attendant, Special Advance, and Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, then died.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuanjia era he rose to Palace Attendant, Special Advance, and Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, then died.

sentences.zh: 初，澹從弟混與劉毅昵，澹常以為憂，漸疏混，每謂弟璞、從子瞻曰：「益壽此性，終當破家。

translations.literal: Earlier, Dan's younger cousin Hun was intimate with Liu Yi; Dan always took this as worry, gradually kept Hun at a distance, and often said to his younger brother Pu and his nephew Zhan, "Yishou by nature will in the end ruin the family."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Dan's younger cousin Hun was intimate with Liu Yi; Dan always worried over this, gradually kept Hun at a distance, and often told his brother Pu and his nephew Zhan, "Yishou by nature will in the end ruin the family."

sentences.zh: 」混尋見誅，朝廷以澹先言，故不及禍。

translations.literal: Hun was soon executed; the court because Dan had spoken first did not extend the disaster to him.
translations.idiomatic: Hun became soon executed; the court because Dan had spoken first did not extend the disaster to him.

sentences.zh: 璞字景山，幼孝友，祖安深賞愛之，位光祿勳。

translations.literal: Pu, styled Jingshan, was filial and fraternal from youth; his grandfather An deeply loved and prized him; he held the post of Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: Pu, courtesy name Jingshan, was filial and fraternal from childhood; his grandfather An deeply loved and prized him; he served as Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 從父 裕

translations.literal: Father's younger cousin Yu
translations.idiomatic: The father's younger cousin, Yu

sentences.zh: 謝裕字景仁，朗弟允之子、而晦從父也。

translations.literal: Xie Yu, styled Jingren, was son of Lang's younger brother Yun and thus Hui's father's younger cousin.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Yu, courtesy name Jingren, was son of Lang's younger brother Yun and thus Hui's father's younger cousin.

sentences.zh: 名與宋武帝諱同，故以字行。

translations.literal: His name matched the taboo of Emperor Wu of Song, so he went by his style.
translations.idiomatic: His given name matched Emperor Wu of Song's taboo, so he went by his courtesy name.

sentences.zh: 允字令度，位宣城內史。

translations.literal: Yun, styled Lingdu, held the post of Interior Administrator of Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yun, courtesy name Lingdu, served as Interior Administrator of Xuancheng.

sentences.zh: 景仁幼為從祖安所知，始為前軍行參軍，會稽王世子元顯嬖人張法順權傾一時，內外無不造門，唯景仁不至，年三十而方為著作佐郎。

translations.literal: Jingren was known from youth by his grand-uncle An; he first served as Army Registrar on the staff of the Forward Army; Zhang Fashun, favorite of the Heir Apparent to the Prince of Kuaiji, Yuanxian, wielded power for a time and none inside or outside did not visit his gate—only Jingren did not go; he was thirty before becoming Assistant Editor in the Editorial Office.
translations.idiomatic: Jingren was known from childhood by his grand-uncle An; he first served as Army Registrar on the staff of the Forward Army; Zhang Fashun, favorite of the Heir Apparent to the Prince of Kuaiji, Yuanxian, wielded power for a time and none inside or outside did not visit his gate—only Jingren did not go; he was thirty before becoming Assistant Editor in the Editorial Office.

sentences.zh: 桓玄誅元顯，見景仁，謂四坐曰：「司馬庶人父子雲何不敗，遂令謝景仁三十而方佐著作郎。

translations.literal: When Huan Xuan executed Yuanxian and saw Jingren, he said to those seated, "How is it the father and son of the Sima commoners did not fall sooner, that they let Xie Jingren reach thirty before assisting as Editorial Lang?"
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Xuan executed Yuanxian and saw Jingren, he said to those seated, "How did the Sima commoners' father and son fail to fall sooner, that Xie Jingren reached thirty before assisting as Editorial Lang?"

sentences.zh: 」玄建楚台，以補黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: When Xuan established the Chu regime, Jingren was appointed Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuan established the Chu regime, Jingren became appointed Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 及篡位，領驍騎將軍。

translations.literal: When he usurped the throne, Jingren held the post of General of Valiant Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuan usurped the throne, Jingren became General of Valiant Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 景仁博聞強識，善敘前言往行，玄每與言不倦。

translations.literal: Jingren was broadly learned with strong memory, skilled at narrating words and deeds of earlier men; Xuan whenever he spoke with him never tired.
translations.idiomatic: Jingren was broadly learned with a strong memory, skilled at narrating words and deeds of earlier men; Xuan never tired of talking with him.

sentences.zh: 玄出行，殷仲文、卞範之之徒皆騎馬散從，而使景仁陪輦。

translations.literal: When Xuan went out, Yin Zhongwen, Bian Fanzhi, and the like all rode scattered in attendance, but had Jingren accompany the carriage.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuan went out, Yin Zhongwen, Bian Fanzhi, and the like rode scattered in attendance, but had Jingren accompany the carriage.

sentences.zh: 宋武帝為桓修撫軍中兵參軍，嘗詣景仁諮事，景仁與語說，因留帝食。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Song, as Army Registrar on Huan Xiu's Pacification Army staff, once went to Jingren to consult on affairs; Jingren conversed with him and kept the Emperor to eat.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu, then Army Registrar on Huan Xiu's Pacification Army staff, once went to Jingren to consult on affairs; Jingren talked with him and kept him to eat.

sentences.zh: 食未辦，而景仁為玄所召。

translations.literal: The food was not yet ready when Jingren was summoned by Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: The meal was not yet ready when Xuan summoned Jingren.

sentences.zh: 玄性促，俄頃間騎詔續至，帝屢求去，景仁不許，曰：「主上見待，要應有方，我欲與客食，豈不得待？

translations.literal: Xuan was impatient by nature; in a short while mounted messengers with imperial orders came in succession; the Emperor repeatedly asked to leave but Jingren would not allow it and said, "When the lord treats one well, there must be a method; I wish to eat with my guest—can I not wait?"
translations.idiomatic: Xuan became impatient by nature; in a short while mounted messengers with imperial orders came in succession; the Emperor repeatedly asked to leave but Jingren would not allow it and said, "When the lord treats one well, there must be a method; I wish to eat with my guest—can I not wait?"

sentences.zh: 」竟安坐飽食然後應召。

translations.literal: He sat at ease, ate his fill, and only then answered the summons.
translations.idiomatic: This man sat at ease, ate his fill, and only then answered the summons.

sentences.zh: 帝甚感之。

translations.literal: The Emperor was deeply moved by this.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 及平建鄴，景仁與百僚同見，武帝目之曰：「此名公孫也。

translations.literal: When Jiankang was pacified, Jingren appeared with the hundred officials; the Emperor looked at him and said, "This is a grandson of a famous house."
translations.idiomatic: When Jiankang became pacified, Jingren appeared with the hundred officials; the Emperor looked at him and said, "This is a grandson of a famous house."

sentences.zh: 」歷位武帝鎮軍司馬，復為車騎司馬。

translations.literal: He held posts in succession as Army Marshal to the Emperor as General Who Guards the Army, then again as Army Marshal to the Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He served in succession as Army Marshal to the General Who Guards the Army, then again as Army Marshal to the Chariots and Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 義熙五年，帝將伐慕容超，朝議皆謂不可，劉毅時鎮姑孰，固止帝，以為「苻堅侵境，謝太傅猶不自行。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yixi the Emperor wished to attack Murong Chao; court debate mostly said it could not be done; Liu Yi then garrisoned Gudu and firmly stopped the Emperor, saying, "When Fu Jian invaded the borders, Grand Tutor Xie still did not go in person.
translations.idiomatic: In Yixi year five the Emperor wished to attack Murong Chao; court debate mostly said it could not be done; Liu Yi, then garrisoning Gudu, firmly stopped him: "When Fu Jian invaded the borders, Grand Tutor Xie still did not go in person.

sentences.zh: 宰相遠出，傾動根本」。

translations.literal: The Chancellor going far out shakes the foundations."
translations.idiomatic: The Chancellor going far afield shakes the foundations."

sentences.zh: 景仁獨曰：「公建桓、文之烈，應天人之心，雖業高振古，而德刑未樹，宜推亡固存，廣振威略。

translations.literal: Jingren alone said, "Your Grace has built the achievement of Duke Huan and Duke Wen and answered the hearts of Heaven and men; though your enterprise towers above the ancients, virtue and punishment are not yet established—you should push the fallen and strengthen what remains, broadly extend your martial prestige.
translations.idiomatic: Jingren alone said, "Your Grace has built the achievement of Duke Huan and Duke Wen and answered the hearts of Heaven and men; though your enterprise towers above the ancients, virtue and punishment are not yet established—you should push the fallen and strengthen what remains and broadly extend your martial prestige.

sentences.zh: 平定之後，養銳息徒，然後觀兵洛汭，修復園寢，豈有縱敵貽患者哉。

translations.literal: After pacification, nurture sharpness and rest the troops; then review the army at the Luo ford and restore the imperial tombs—how could there be letting the enemy remain to bring future harm?"
translations.idiomatic: After pacification, nurture sharpness and rest the troops; then review the army at the Luo ford and restore the imperial tombs—how could you leave the enemy standing to bring future harm?"

sentences.zh: 」帝從之。

translations.literal: The Emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor followed his counsel.

sentences.zh: 及北伐，大司馬琅邪王天子母弟，屬當儲副，帝深以根本為憂，轉景仁大司馬左司馬，專總府任。

translations.literal: On the northern expedition, the Grand Marshal, Prince of Langye, the Son of Heaven's younger brother by the same mother, was the proper heir; the Emperor deeply worried over the foundations and transferred Jingren to Left Army Marshal of the Grand Marshal's office, with sole charge of the headquarters duties.
translations.idiomatic: On the northern expedition, the Grand Marshal, Prince of Langye, the Son of Heaven's younger brother by the same mother, became the proper heir; the Emperor deeply worried over the foundations and transferred Jingren to Left Army Marshal of the Grand Marshal's office, with sole charge of the headquarters duties.

sentences.zh: 又遷吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He was also transferred to Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was also made Director of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 時從兄混為尚書左僕射，依制不得相監，帝啟依僕射王彪之、尚書王劭前例不解職。

translations.literal: At the time his elder cousin Hun was Vice Director of the Masters of Writing; by regulation they could not supervise each other, but the Emperor memorialized following the earlier precedents of Vice Director Wang Biaozhi and Director Wang Shao in not leaving office.
translations.idiomatic: Then his elder cousin Hun was Vice Director of the Masters of Writing; by regulation they could not supervise each other, but the Emperor memorialized following the earlier precedents of Vice Director Wang Biaozhi and Director Wang Shao in not leaving office.

sentences.zh: 坐選吏部令史邢安泰為都令史、平原太守，二官共除，安泰以令史職拜謁陵廟，為御史中丞鄭鮮之所糾，白衣領職。

translations.literal: For appointing Ministry of Personnel clerk Xing Antai as Chief Clerk and Administrator of Pingyuan—two offices at once—and Antai, in the clerk's capacity, paying respects at the imperial tombs, he was impeached by Censor-in-Chief Zheng Xianzhi and served in office in plain clothes.
translations.idiomatic: For appointing Ministry clerk Xing Antai as Chief Clerk and Administrator of Pingyuan at once—and Antai, in his clerk's capacity, paying respects at the imperial tombs—he was impeached by Censor-in-Chief Zheng Xianzhi and served in plain clothes.

sentences.zh: 十一年，為左僕射。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he became Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: In year eleven he became Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 景仁性矜嚴整潔，居宇淨麗，每唾輒唾左右人衣，事畢，即聽一日澣濯。

translations.literal: Jingren's nature was stern, neat, and fastidious; his dwelling was clean and bright; whenever he spat he spat on the clothes of attendants at his side, and when the matter was done he allowed them one day's washing.
translations.idiomatic: Jingren's nature became stern, neat, and fastidious; his dwelling was clean and bright; whenever he spat he spat on the clothes of attendants at his side, and when the matter was done he allowed them one day's washing.

sentences.zh: 每欲唾，左右爭來受之。

translations.literal: Whenever he was about to spit, attendants vied to receive it.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he was about to spit, attendants vied to catch it.

sentences.zh: 武帝雅相知重，申以昏姻，廬陵王義真妃，景仁女也。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu knew and valued him deeply and joined him by marriage; Prince Yizhen of Luling's consort was Jingren's daughter.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu knew and valued him deeply and joined him by marriage; Prince Yizhen of Luling's consort became Jingren's daughter.

sentences.zh: 十二年卒，贈金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he died and was posthumously titled Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: In year twelve he died and was posthumously titled Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 葬日，武帝親臨甚慟。

translations.literal: On the burial day the Emperor came in person and grieved deeply.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of burial Emperor Wu came in person and mourned deeply.

sentences.zh: 子恂字泰溫，位鄱陽太守。

translations.literal: His son Xun, styled Taiwen, held the post of Administrator of Poyang.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xun, courtesy name Taiwen, served as Administrator of Poyang.

sentences.zh: 恂子孺子，少與族兄莊齊名。

translations.literal: Xun's son Ruzi was young together with his clansman elder brother Zhuang and equally famed.
translations.idiomatic: Xun's son Ruzi grew up alongside his clansman Zhuang and shared equal fame.

sentences.zh: 多藝能，尤善聲律。

translations.literal: He had many arts and skills and was especially skilled in tonal rules.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered many arts and was especially skilled in tonal rules.

sentences.zh: 車騎將軍王彧，孺子姑之子也。

translations.literal: Chariots and Cavalry General Wang Yu was son of Ruzi's aunt.
translations.idiomatic: Chariots and Cavalry General Wang Yu became son of Ruzi's aunt.

sentences.zh: 嘗與孺子宴桐台，孺子吹笙，彧自起舞，既而歎曰：「今日真使人飄颻有伊、洛間意。

translations.literal: Once he banqueted with Ruzi at Tongtai Terrace; Ruzi played the sheng and Yu rose to dance, then sighed and said, "Today truly makes one feel buoyant, as though between the Yi and Luo.
translations.idiomatic: Once he banqueted with Ruzi at Tongtai Terrace; Ruzi played the sheng and Yu rose to dance, then sighed: "Today truly makes one feel buoyant, as though between the Yi and Luo.

sentences.zh: 」為新安王主簿，出為廬江郡，辭，宋孝武謂有司曰：「謝孺子不可屈為小郡。

translations.literal: He was Chief Clerk to Prince Xin'an, then went out as Administrator of Lujiang; he declined, and Emperor Xiaowu of Song told the relevant offices, "Xie Ruzi cannot be reduced to a small commandery."
translations.idiomatic: This man was Chief Clerk to Prince Xin'an, then went out as Administrator of Lujiang; he declined, and Emperor Xiaowu of Song told the relevant offices, "Xie Ruzi cannot be reduced to a small commandery."

sentences.zh: 」乃以為司徒主簿。

translations.literal: He was therefore made Chief Clerk to the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: This man was therefore made Chief Clerk to the Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 後以家貧，求西陽太守，卒官。

translations.literal: Later, because his family was poor, he sought the post of Administrator of Xiyang and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Later, because his family was poor, he sought the post of Administrator of Xiyang and died while still in office.

sentences.zh: 子璟，少與從叔朓俱知名。

translations.literal: His son Jing was young together with his father's younger cousin Tiao and both were known.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jing grew up with his father's younger cousin Tiao and both were known.

sentences.zh: 齊竟陵王子良開西邸，招文學，璟亦預焉。

translations.literal: Prince Ziliang of Jingling of Qi opened the Western Lodge and gathered literary men; Jing also took part.
translations.idiomatic: Jing also took part.; prince Ziliang of Jingling of Qi opened the Western Lodge and gathered literary men

sentences.zh: 位中書郎。

translations.literal: He held the post of Attendant Gentleman of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Attendant Gentleman of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 梁天監中，為左戶尚書，再遷侍中，固辭年老求金紫，帝不悅，未敘，會卒。

translations.literal: In the Tianjian era of Liang he was Director of the Left Household, then promoted again to Palace Attendant; he firmly declined, citing old age and seeking the golden seal and purple ribbon; the Emperor was displeased and did not grant rank; he died before promotion.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianjian era of Liang he became Director of the Left Household, then promoted again to Palace Attendant; he firmly declined, citing old age and seeking the golden seal and purple ribbon; the Emperor was displeased and did not grant rank; he died before promotion.

sentences.zh: 純字景懋，景仁弟也。

translations.literal: Chun, styled Jingmao, was Jingren's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Chun, courtesy name Jingmao, was Jingren's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 劉毅鎮江陵，以為衛軍長史、南平相。

translations.literal: When Liu Yi garrisoned Jiangling, Chun was made Chief Clerk to the Guard Army and Chancellor of Nanping.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yi garrisoned Jiangling, Chun became made Chief Clerk to the Guard Army and Chancellor of Nanping.

sentences.zh: 及王鎮惡襲毅，毅時病，佐史聞兵至，馳還入府，左右引車欲還外廨，純叱之曰：「我人吏也，逃欲安之。

translations.literal: When Wang Zhen'e attacked Yi, Yi was then ill; a clerk heard the army had arrived, galloped back into the headquarters, and attendants drew the carriage wanting to return to the outer office; Chun shouted at them, "I am this man's official—where would I flee?
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Zhen'e attacked Yi, Yi became then ill; a clerk heard the army had arrived, galloped back into the headquarters, and attendants drew the carriage wanting to return to the outer office; Chun shouted at them, "I am this man's official—where would I flee?

sentences.zh: 」及入，毅兵敗眾散，純為人所殺。

translations.literal: When he entered, Yi's army was defeated and the host scattered; Chun was killed by others.
translations.idiomatic: When he entered, Yi's army was defeated and the host scattered; Chun was killed.

sentences.zh: 純弟甝字景甝，位司徒右長史。

translations.literal: Chun's younger brother Lin, styled Jinglin, held the post of Right Chief Clerk to the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Chun's younger brother Lin, courtesy name Jinglin, served as Right Chief Clerk to the Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 甝弟述字景先，小字道兒。

translations.literal: Lin's younger brother Shu, styled Jingxian, childhood name Dao'er.
translations.idiomatic: Lin's younger brother Shu, courtesy name Jingxian, childhood name Dao'er.

sentences.zh: 少有至行，隨純在江陵，純遇害，述奉純喪還都，至西塞遇暴風，純喪舫流漂不知所在，述乘小船尋求，經純妻庾舫過。

translations.literal: From youth he had utmost conduct; following Chun in Jiangling, when Chun was killed Shu escorted Chun's coffin back to the capital; at Xisai they met violent wind, Chun's funeral barge drifted away and its whereabouts were unknown; Shu took a small boat to search, passing the barge of Chun's wife Lady Yu.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he had utmost conduct; following Chun in Jiangling, when Chun became killed Shu escorted Chun's coffin back to the capital; at Xisai they met violent wind, Chun's funeral barge drifted away and its whereabouts were unknown; Shu took a small boat to search, passing the barge of Chun's wife Lady Yu.

sentences.zh: 庾遣人謂曰：「小郎去必無及，寧可存亡俱盡邪。

translations.literal: Yu sent someone to say, "The young master going will surely not reach them—would you rather both perish together?
translations.idiomatic: Yu sent word: "The young master going will surely not reach them—would you rather both perish together?

sentences.zh: 」述號泣答曰：「若安全至岸，尚須營理；

translations.literal: Shu wept and answered, "If they safely reach shore, there will still be arrangements to make;
translations.idiomatic: "If they safely reach shore, there will still be arrangements to make;, shu wept and answered

sentences.zh: 如其已致意外，述亦無心獨存。

translations.literal: if they have already met mishap, Shu has no heart to live alone.
translations.idiomatic: if they have already met mishap, I have no heart to live alone.

sentences.zh: 」因冒浪而進，見純喪幾沒，述號叫呼天，幸而獲免。

translations.literal: He then braved the waves and advanced; he saw Chun's coffin nearly submerged, cried out to Heaven, and by fortune escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Then he braved the waves and advanced; he saw Chun's coffin nearly submerged, cried out to Heaven, and by fortune escaped.

sentences.zh: 咸以為精誠所致，武帝聞而嘉之。

translations.literal: All thought it due to utmost sincerity; Emperor Wu heard and praised him.
translations.idiomatic: All attributed it to utmost sincerity; Emperor Wu heard and praised him.

sentences.zh: 及臨豫州，諷中正以為迎主簿，甚被器遇。

translations.literal: When he arrived at Yuzhou, the provincial appraiser was urged to make him Chief Clerk to welcome the governor; he was greatly valued.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived at Yuzhou, the provincial appraiser became urged to make him Chief Clerk to welcome the governor; he was greatly valued.

sentences.zh: 景仁愛甝而憎述，嘗設饌請宋武帝，希命甝豫坐，而帝召述。

translations.literal: Jingren loved Lin but disliked Shu; once he set out a feast and invited Emperor Wu, hoping to have Lin join the seating, but the Emperor summoned Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Jingren loved Lin but disliked Shu; once he set a feast and invited Emperor Wu, hoping Lin would join the seating, but the Emperor summoned Shu.

sentences.zh: 述知非景仁夙意，又慮帝命之，請急不從。

translations.literal: Shu knew this was not Jingren's old intent and also feared the Emperor's command; he urgently begged off and was not obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: Shu knew this became not Jingren's old intent and also feared the Emperor's command; he urgently begged off and was not obeyed.

sentences.zh: 帝馳遣呼述，須至乃飧，其見重如此。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent a fast messenger to summon Shu and would not eat until he arrived—such was the esteem.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent a fast messenger to summon Shu and would not eat until he arrived—such was the esteem in which he was held.

sentences.zh: 及景仁疾，述盡心視湯藥，飲食必嘗而後進。

translations.literal: When Jingren fell ill, Shu devoted himself to tending medicines and broth, always tasting before presenting.
translations.idiomatic: After Jingren fell ill, Shu devoted himself to tending medicines and broth, always tasting before presenting.

sentences.zh: 衣不解帶不盥櫛者累旬，景仁深感愧焉，友愛遂篤。

translations.literal: For many tens of days he did not loosen his belt or wash or comb; Jingren was deeply ashamed and their brotherly love became thick.
translations.idiomatic: For many tens of days he did not loosen his belt or wash or comb; Jingren was deeply ashamed and their brotherly love became deep.

sentences.zh: 及景仁卒，哀號過禮。

translations.literal: When Jingren died, his wailing exceeded the rites.
translations.idiomatic: After Jingren died, his wailing exceeded the rites.

sentences.zh: 景仁肥壯，買材數具皆不合用，述哀惶，親選乃獲焉。

translations.literal: Jingren was stout; several sets of coffin timber bought were all unsuitable; Shu in grief and panic personally chose until he obtained fit timber.
translations.idiomatic: Jingren became stout; several sets of coffin timber bought were all unsuitable; Shu in grief and panic personally chose until he obtained fit timber.

sentences.zh: 為太尉參軍，從征司馬休之，封吉陽縣五等侯。

translations.literal: He was Staff Officer to the Grand Marshal and followed the campaign against Sima Xiuzhi; he was enfeoffed as fifth-rank Marquis of Jiyang County.
translations.idiomatic: He was Staff Officer to the Grand Marshal and followed the campaign against Sima Xiuzhi; he received enfeoffment as fifth-rank Marquis of Jiyang County.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二年，拜中書侍郎。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanjia he was appointed Gentleman of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia year two he was appointed Gentleman of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 後為彭城王義康驃騎長史，領南郡太守。

translations.literal: Later he was Chief Clerk to Prince Yikang of Pengcheng's Cavalry General staff and concurrently Administrator of Nan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward, he was Chief Clerk to Prince Yikang of Pengcheng's Cavalry General staff and concurrently Administrator of Nan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 義康入相，述又為司徒左長史，轉左衛將軍。

translations.literal: When Yikang entered the chancellery, Shu was again Left Chief Clerk to the Minister of Education, then transferred to General of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Yikang entered the chancellery, Shu became again Left Chief Clerk to the Minister of Education, then transferred to General of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 蒞官清約，私無宅舍，義康遇之甚厚。

translations.literal: In office he was pure and sparing; privately he had no dwelling; Yikang treated him very generously.
translations.idiomatic: In office he became pure and sparing; privately he had no dwelling; Yikang treated him very generously.

sentences.zh: 尚書僕射殷景仁、領軍將軍劉湛並與述為異常之交。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Yin Jingren and General Who Leads the Army Liu Zhan were both in extraordinary friendship with Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Yin Jingren and General Who Leads the Army Liu Zhan were both in extraordinary friendship with Shu.

sentences.zh: 述美風姿，善舉止，湛每謂人曰：「我見謝道兒未嘗足。

translations.literal: Shu had fine bearing and graceful conduct; Zhan often told people, "When I see Xie Dao'er I never have my fill.
translations.idiomatic: Shu bore himself beautifully and graceful conduct; Zhan often told people, "When I see Xie Dao'er I never have my fill.

sentences.zh: 」雍州刺史張邵以黷貨將致大辟，述表陳邵先朝舊勳，宜蒙優貸，文帝手詔詶納焉。

translations.literal: Yong Province Inspector Zhang Shao for corrupt taking was about to receive capital punishment; Shu memorialized that Shao had merit in earlier dynasties and should receive lenient treatment; Emperor Wen personally wrote in reply and accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Yong Inspector Zhang Shao, for corrupt taking, was about to receive capital punishment; Shu memorialized that Shao had merit in earlier dynasties and should receive lenient treatment; Emperor Wen personally wrote in reply and accepted.

sentences.zh: 述語子綜曰：「主上矜邵夙誠，自將曲恕，吾所啟謬會，故特見納。

translations.literal: Shu told his son Zong, "The lord pities Shao's old loyalty and will himself show clemency; my memorial happened to agree, and so was specially accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Shu told his son Zong, "The lord pities Shao's old loyalty and will himself show clemency; my memorial happened to agree, and so became specially accepted.

sentences.zh: 若此跡宣佈，則為侵奪主恩。

translations.literal: If this trace were broadcast, it would be seizing the lord's grace.
translations.idiomatic: If this were broadcast, it would be seizing the lord's grace.

sentences.zh: 」使綜對前焚之。

translations.literal: He had Zong face forward and burn it.
translations.idiomatic: This man had Zong face forward and burn it.

sentences.zh: 帝后謂邵曰：「卿之獲免，謝述力焉。」

translations.literal: The Emperor later told Shao, "Your escape—Xie Shu made it happen."
translations.idiomatic: "Your escape—Xie Shu made it happen.", the Emperor later told Shao

sentences.zh: 述有心虛疾，性理時或乖謬，卒于吳興太守。

translations.literal: Shu had an illness of the heart with vacuity; his temperament sometimes went awry; he died as Administrator of Wuxing.
