translations.idiomatic: Shu had an illness of heart vacuity; his temperament sometimes went awry; he died as Administrator of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 喪還未至都數十里，殷景仁、劉湛同乘迎赴，望船流涕。

translations.literal: When the coffin had not yet reached the capital by several tens of li, Yin Jingren and Liu Zhan rode together to meet it and wept at the sight of the boat.
translations.idiomatic: Before the coffin had reached the capital by several tens of li, Yin Jingren and Liu Zhan rode together to meet it and wept at the sight of the boat.

sentences.zh: 及劉湛誅，義康外鎮，將行歎曰：「謝述唯勸吾退，劉湛唯勸吾進，述亡而湛存，吾所以得罪也。

translations.literal: When Liu Zhan was executed and Yikang went out to a regional post, about to leave he sighed, "Xie Shu only urged me to withdraw; Liu Zhan only urged me to advance—Shu dead and Zhan living, that is why I have offended.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Zhan was put to death and Yikang went out to a regional post, about to leave he sighed, "Xie Shu only urged me to withdraw; Liu Zhan only urged me to advance—Shu dead and Zhan living, that is why I have offended.

sentences.zh: 」文帝亦曰：「謝述若存，義康必不至此。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen also said, "If Xie Shu still lived, Yikang would not have come to this.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen also said, "If Xie Shu were still alive, Yikang would not have come to this."

sentences.zh: 」三子：綜、約、緯。

translations.literal: Three sons: Zong, Yue, and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons: Zong, Yue, and Wei.

sentences.zh: 綜有才藝，善隸書，為太子中舍人。

translations.literal: Zong had talent and skill, wrote clerical script well, and was Attendant of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Zong had talent and skill, wrote clerical script well, and served as Attendant of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 與范曄謀反伏誅；

translations.literal: He plotted rebellion with Fan Ye and was executed;
translations.idiomatic: This man plotted rebellion with Fan Ye and was executed;

sentences.zh: 約亦死。

translations.literal: Yue also died.
translations.idiomatic: Yue also died.

sentences.zh: 緯尚宋文帝第五女長城公主，素為綜、約所憎，免死，徙廣州，孝建中還都。

translations.literal: Wei married the fifth daughter of Emperor Wen of Song, Princess Great Wall; he had always been hated by Zong and Yue, was spared death, and was banished to Guangzhou; in the Xiaojian era he returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Wei married the fifth daughter of Emperor Wen of Song, Princess Great Wall; he had always been hated by Zong and Yue, became spared death, and was banished to Guangzhou; in the Xiaojian era he returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 方雅有父風，位正員郎。

translations.literal: Fangya had his father's bearing and held the post of Regular Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Fangya had his father's bearing and served as Regular Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 子朓。

translations.literal: His son Tiao.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tiao.

sentences.zh: 朓字玄暉，少好學，有美名，文章清麗。

translations.literal: Tiao, styled Xuanhui, loved learning from youth and had a fine reputation; his writing was clear and beautiful.
translations.idiomatic: Tiao, courtesy name Xuanhui, loved learning from childhood and had a fine reputation; his writing was clear and beautiful.

sentences.zh: 為齊隨王子隆鎮西功曹，轉文學。

translations.literal: He was Merit Officer on Prince Zilong of Qi's Pacification of the West staff, then transferred to Literary Officer.
translations.idiomatic: This man was Merit Officer on Prince Zilong of Qi's Pacification of the West staff, then transferred to Literary Officer.

sentences.zh: 子隆在荊州，好辭賦，朓尤被賞，不舍日夕。

translations.literal: Zilong in Jing Province loved rhapsodies and fu; Tiao was especially prized and was never apart day or night.
translations.idiomatic: Zilong in Jing Province loved rhapsodies and fu; Tiao became especially prized and was never apart day or night.

sentences.zh: 長史王秀之以朓年少相動，欲以啟聞。

translations.literal: Chief Clerk Wang Xiuzhi because Tiao was young wanted to move against him and report this to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Clerk Wang Xiuzhi, because Tiao was young, wanted to move against him and report to the throne.

sentences.zh: 朓知之，因事求還，道中為詩寄西府曰：「常恐鷹隼擊，時菊委嚴霜，寄言罻羅者，寥廓已高翔。

translations.literal: Tiao knew this and on a pretext asked to return; on the road he composed a poem to send to the Western Headquarters: "I often fear the hawk and falcon's strike, when chrysanthemums bow to harsh frost; I send word to the fowlers—the vast sky has already soared high.
translations.idiomatic: Tiao knew this and on a pretext asked to return; on the road he composed a poem to the Western Headquarters: "I often fear the hawk and falcon's strike, when chrysanthemums bow to harsh frost; I send word to the fowlers—the vast sky has already soared high.

sentences.zh: 」是也。

translations.literal: Such was the poem.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the poem.

sentences.zh: 仍除新安王中軍記室。

translations.literal: He was then made Recorder to Prince Xin'an's Central Army.
translations.idiomatic: This man was then made Recorder to Prince Xin'an's Central Army.

sentences.zh: 朓箋辭子隆曰：朓聞潢汙之水，思朝宗而每竭，駑蹇之乘，希沃若而中疲。

translations.literal: Tiao submitted a letter declining Zilong, saying: Tiao has heard that muddy waters think of flowing toward the great river yet are always exhausted, and a lame nag hopes for the great rain yet fails midway.
translations.idiomatic: Tiao submitted a letter declining Zilong: "I have heard that muddy waters think of flowing toward the great river yet are always exhausted, and a lame nag hopes for the great rain yet fails midway.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 皋壤搖落，對之惆悵，歧路東西，或以嗚唈。

translations.literal: The frost-bitten fields stir melancholy; east and west at the crossroads, one sometimes weeps aloud.
translations.idiomatic: That frost-bitten fields stir melancholy; east and west at the crossroads, one sometimes weeps aloud.

sentences.zh: 況乃服義徒擁，歸志莫從，邈若墜雨，飄似秋蔕。

translations.literal: How much more when duty binds the heart yet the will to return has nowhere to follow—distant as falling rain, drifting as autumn fruit stem.
translations.idiomatic: How much more when duty binds the heart yet the will to return has nowhere to follow—distant as falling rain, drifting as an autumn fruit stem.

sentences.zh: 朓實庸流，行能無算，屬天地休明，山川受納，褒采一介，搜揚小善，故得舍耒場圃，奉筆兔園。

translations.literal: Tiao is truly a common stream, his conduct and capacity beyond reckoning; yet Heaven and earth are bright and mountains and rivers receive all—one meager gift was sought, one small good was lifted—therefore I could leave the field and garden and take up brush in the Rabbit Garden.
translations.idiomatic: Tiao is truly a common stream, his conduct and capacity beyond reckoning; yet Heaven and earth are bright and mountains and rivers receive all—one meager gift became sought, one small good was lifted—therefore I could leave the field and garden and take up brush in the Rabbit Garden.

sentences.zh: 東泛三江，西浮七澤，契闊戎旃，從容燕語。

translations.literal: East I floated the Three Rivers, west the Seven Marshes; parting and joining under campaign banners, at ease in banquet talk.
translations.idiomatic: I floated east on the Three Rivers and west on the Seven Marshes; parting and joining under campaign banners, at ease in banquet talk.

sentences.zh: 長裾日曳，後乘載脂，榮立府廷，恩加顏色，沐發晞陽，未測涯涘，撫臆論報，早誓肌骨。

translations.literal: Long robe trailing day by day, rear carriage loaded with grease; glory standing in the headquarters hall, favor added to my face; hair washed in the morning sun, the shore not yet measured; hand on breast speaking repayment, early sworn in flesh and bone.
translations.idiomatic: Long robe trailing day by day, rear carriage loaded with grease; glory standing in the headquarters hall, favor added to my face; hair washed in the morning sun, the shore not yet measured; hand on breast speaking repayment, sworn early in flesh and bone.

sentences.zh: 不悟滄溟未運，波臣自蕩，渤澥方春，旅翮先謝。

translations.literal: I did not perceive the blue sea not yet crossed, the wave-subject already scattered; the Bohai Sea just in spring, the traveler's wing first withered.
translations.idiomatic: I did not yet see the blue sea crossed when the wave-subject already scattered; the Bohai Sea was just in spring, yet the traveler's wing had already withered.

sentences.zh: 清切蕃房，寂寥舊蓽，輕舟反泝，吊影獨留。

translations.literal: The clear and close lodge of the headquarters, the old hut now lonely; light boat turning back upstream, I mourn my shadow left alone.
translations.idiomatic: That clear and close lodge of the headquarters, the old hut now lonely; light boat turning back upstream, I mourn my shadow left alone.

sentences.zh: 白雲在天，龍門不見，去德滋永，思德滋深。

translations.literal: White clouds in the sky, the Dragon Gate unseen; virtue departed ever longer, thought of virtue ever deeper.
translations.idiomatic: White clouds hang in the sky and the Dragon Gate is unseen; virtue departed grows ever longer, and thought of virtue grows ever deeper.

sentences.zh: 唯待青江可望，候歸艎於春渚，朱邸方開，效蓬心於秋實。

translations.literal: Only wait until the blue river can be seen and the returning boat awaited at the spring ford; when the vermilion residence opens wide, offer the humble heart like autumn fruit.
translations.idiomatic: I only wait until the blue river comes into view and the returning boat can be awaited at the spring ford; when the vermilion residence opens wide, I will offer my humble heart like autumn fruit.

sentences.zh: 如其簪屨或存，衽席無改，雖復身填溝壑，猶望妻子知歸。

translations.literal: If hairpin and shoes still remain, mat and seat unchanged, though body fill ditch and gully, I still hope wife and children know the way home.
translations.idiomatic: If hairpin and shoes still remain and mat and seat are unchanged, though my body may fill ditch and gully, I still hope my wife and children will know the way home.

sentences.zh: 攬涕告辭，悲來橫集。

translations.literal: Gathering tears to take leave, grief comes crossing horizontal.
translations.idiomatic: Gathering tears to take my leave, grief came flooding in.

sentences.zh: 時荊州信去倚待，朓執筆便成，文無點易。

translations.literal: At the time a messenger from Jing Province was waiting; Tiao took brush and it was finished at once, the text without a dot changed.
translations.idiomatic: At the time a messenger from Jing Province was waiting; Tiao took brush and finished at once, the text without a dot changed.

sentences.zh: 以本官兼尚書殿中郎。

translations.literal: With his original office he was also Gentleman of the Palace Department of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: With his original office he became also Gentleman of the Palace Department of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 隆昌初，敕朓接北使，朓自以口訥，啟讓，見許。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longchang an order had Tiao receive the northern envoys; Tiao himself thought his speech slow and memorialized to decline; permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Longchang an order had Tiao receive the northern envoys; Tiao himself thought his speech slow and memorialized to decline; permission became granted.

sentences.zh: 明帝輔政，以為驃騎諮議，領記室，掌霸府文筆。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming assisted in government, Tiao was made Staff Officer to the Cavalry General and Recorder, in charge of the hegemon's office writing.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming assisted in government, Tiao became made Staff Officer to the Cavalry General and Recorder, in charge of the hegemon's office writing.

sentences.zh: 又掌中書詔誥，轉中書郎。

translations.literal: He also managed Secretariat edicts and proclamations, then transferred to Gentleman of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He likewise managed Secretariat edicts and proclamations, then transferred to Gentleman of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 出為晉安王鎮北諮議、南東海太守，行南徐州事。

translations.literal: He went out as Staff Officer to Prince Jin'an's Pacification of the North and Administrator of East Sea, acting for South Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: This man went out as Staff Officer to Prince Jin'an's Pacification of the North and Administrator of East Sea, acting for South Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 啟王敬則反謀，上甚賞之，遷尚書吏部郎。

translations.literal: He reported Wang Jingze's plot to rebel; the Emperor greatly praised him and promoted him to Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: This man reported Wang Jingze's plot to rebel; the Emperor greatly praised him and promoted him to Director of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 朓上表三讓。

translations.literal: Tiao submitted a memorial declining three times.
translations.idiomatic: Tiao memorialized three times to decline the appointment.

sentences.zh: 中書疑朓官未及讓，以問國子祭酒沈約。

translations.literal: The Secretariat doubted Tiao's office had not yet reached the point of declining and asked Grand Master of the National University Shen Yue.
translations.idiomatic: That Secretariat doubted Tiao's office had not yet reached the point of declining and asked Grand Master of the National University Shen Yue.

sentences.zh: 約曰：「宋元嘉中，范曄讓吏部，朱修之讓黃門，蔡興宗讓中書，並三表詔答。

translations.literal: Yue said, "In the Yuanjia era of Song, Fan Ye declined the Ministry of Personnel, Zhu Xiuzhi declined the Yellow Gate, and Cai Xingzong declined the Secretariat—all three memorials received edict replies.
translations.idiomatic: Yue said, "In Song's Yuanjia era, Fan Ye declined the Ministry of Personnel, Zhu Xiuzhi declined the Yellow Gate, and Cai Xingzong declined the Secretariat—all three memorials received edict replies.

sentences.zh: 近代小官不讓，遂成恒俗，恐有乖讓意。

translations.literal: In recent times small offices do not decline—it has become constant custom; I fear this goes against the intent of yielding.
translations.idiomatic: I fear this goes against the intent of yielding.; in recent times small offices do not decline—it has become constant custom

sentences.zh: 王藍田、劉安西並貴重，初自不讓，今豈可慕此不讓邪？

translations.literal: Wang Lantian and Liu Anxi were both honored and weighty and from the first did not decline—how can one now admire this non-declining?
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lantian and Liu Anxi were both men of weight and from the first never declined—how can one now take this refusal to decline as a model?

sentences.zh: 孫興公、孔覬並讓記室，今豈可三署皆讓邪？

translations.literal: Sun Xinggong and Kong Xian both declined the recorder's post—how can all three offices now decline?
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xinggong and Kong Xian both declined the recorder post—how can all three offices now be declined?

sentences.zh: 謝吏部今授超階，讓別有意，豈關官之大小。

translations.literal: Director Xie now receives a leap in rank; the decline has a separate intent—not related to the size of the office.
translations.idiomatic: The decline has a separate intent—not related to the size of the office.; director Xie now receives a leap in rank

sentences.zh: 撝謙之美，本出人情，若大官必讓，便與詣闕章表不異。

translations.literal: The beauty of yielding comes from human feeling; if great offices must decline, it is no different from memorials at the palace gate.
translations.idiomatic: That beauty of yielding comes from human feeling; if great offices must decline, it is no different from memorials at the palace gate.

sentences.zh: 例既如此，謂都非疑。

translations.literal: The precedents being thus, I say there is no doubt in the matter.
translations.idiomatic: That precedents being thus, I say there is no doubt in the matter.

sentences.zh: 」朓讓，優答不許。

translations.literal: Tiao declined; a gracious reply did not permit.
translations.idiomatic: A gracious reply did not permit.; tiao declined

sentences.zh: 朓善草隸，長五言詩，沈約常云：「二百年來無此詩也」。

translations.literal: Tiao was skilled in draft clerical script and long pentasyllabic poetry; Shen Yue often said, "In two hundred years there has been no poetry like this.
translations.idiomatic: Tiao became skilled in draft clerical script and long pentasyllabic poetry; Shen Yue often said, "In two hundred years there has been no poetry like this.

sentences.zh: 敬皇后遷祔山陵，朓撰哀策文，齊世莫有及者。

translations.literal: When the Honored Empress was moved to join the mountain tomb, Tiao composed the lamentation text; in the Qi age none matched him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Honored Empress became moved to join the mountain tomb, Tiao composed the lamentation text; in the Qi age none matched him.

sentences.zh: 東昏失德，江祏欲立江夏王寶玄，末更回惑，與弟祀密謂朓曰：「江夏年少，脫不堪，不可復行廢立。

translations.literal: When Emperor Donghun lost virtue, Jiang Shi wished to establish Prince BaoXuan of Jiangxia; later he wavered again and secretly told Tiao with his brother Si, "Prince Jiangxia is young; if he cannot bear it, we cannot again carry out deposition and establishment.
translations.idiomatic: At the time when Emperor Donghun lost virtue, Jiang Shi wished to establish Prince BaoXuan of Jiangxia; later he wavered again and secretly told Tiao with his brother Si, "Prince Jiangxia is young; if he cannot bear it, we cannot again carry out deposition and establishment.

sentences.zh: 始安年長入纂，不乖物望。

translations.literal: Prince Shi'an is older and succeeds—he does not go against public expectation.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Shi'an is older and would succeed—he would not go against what the world expects.

sentences.zh: 非以此要富貴，只求安國家爾。

translations.literal: It is not that we seek wealth and honor—we only seek to settle the state.
translations.idiomatic: We do not seek wealth and rank by this—we only want to settle the state.

sentences.zh: 」遙光又遣親人劉渢致意於朓。

translations.literal: Yaoguang also sent his close man Liu Wen to convey intent to Tiao.
translations.idiomatic: Yaoguang also sent his confidant Liu Wen to convey his meaning to Tiao.

sentences.zh: 朓自以受恩明帝，不肯答。

translations.literal: Tiao himself thought he had received Emperor Ming's grace and would not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Tiao, believing himself indebted to Emperor Ming, refused to answer.

sentences.zh: 少日，遙光以朓兼知衛尉事，朓懼見引，即以祏等謀告左興盛，又說劉暄曰：「始安一旦南面，則劉渢、劉晏居卿今地，但以卿為反復人爾。

translations.literal: After a few days Yaoguang had Tiao also manage the Commandant of the Guard's affairs; Tiao feared being drawn in and reported the plot of Shi and the others to Zuo Xingsheng, and also told Liu Xuan, "If Prince Shi'an faces south one day, then Liu Wen and Liu Yan will occupy your present posts—you will only be counted a turncoat.
translations.idiomatic: After a few days Yaoguang had Tiao also manage the Commandant of the Guard's affairs; Tiao feared being drawn in and reported the plot of Shi and the others to Zuo Xingsheng, and also told Liu Xuan, "If Prince Shi'an faces south one day, Liu Wen and Liu Yan will occupy your present posts—you will only be counted a turncoat.

sentences.zh: 」暄陽驚，馳告始安王及江祏。

translations.literal: Xuan pretended alarm and galloped to tell Prince Shi'an and Jiang Shi.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan feigned alarm and rode posthaste to inform Prince Shi'an and Jiang Shi.

sentences.zh: 始安欲出朓為東陽郡，祏固執不與。

translations.literal: Prince Shi'an wished to send Tiao out as Administrator of Dongyang; Shi firmly would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: Shi firmly would not allow it.; prince Shi'an wished to send Tiao out as Administrator of Dongyang

sentences.zh: 先是，朓常輕祏為人，祏常詣朓，朓因言有一詩，呼左右取，既而便停。

translations.literal: Earlier Tiao often looked down on Shi as a man; Shi often visited Tiao; Tiao then said he had a poem, called attendants to fetch it, then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Tiao often looked down on Shi; Shi often visited Tiao; Tiao then said he had a poem, called attendants to fetch it, then stopped.

sentences.zh: 祏問其故，云：「定復不急」。

translations.literal: Shi asked the reason; he said, "It surely is not urgent.
translations.idiomatic: Shi asked why; he said, "It surely is not urgent.

sentences.zh: 祏以為輕己。

translations.literal: Shi took this as slighting himself.
translations.idiomatic: Shi took this as a slight against himself.

sentences.zh: 後祏及弟祀、劉渢、劉晏俱候朓，朓謂祏曰：「可謂帶二江之雙流」，以嘲弄之。

translations.literal: Later Shi and his younger brother Si, Liu Wen, and Liu Yan all waited on Tiao; Tiao said to Shi, "One may call this the twin streams carrying two rivers," mocking them.
translations.idiomatic: Later Shi and his brother Si, Liu Wen, and Liu Yan all waited on Tiao; Tiao said to Shi, "One may call this the twin streams carrying two rivers," mocking them.

sentences.zh: 祏轉不堪，至是構而害之。

translations.literal: Shi became ever more unable to bear it; at this he framed him and had him killed.
translations.idiomatic: At this he framed him and had him killed.; shi became ever more unable to bear it

sentences.zh: 詔暴其過惡，收付廷尉。

translations.literal: An edict proclaimed his crimes; he was seized and handed to the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: An edict proclaimed his crimes; he became seized and handed to the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 又使御史中丞範岫奏收朓，下獄死，時年三十六。

translations.literal: The Censor-in-Chief Fan Xiu also memorialized to seize Tiao; he was imprisoned and executed; he was thirty-six.
translations.idiomatic: That Censor-in-Chief Fan Xiu also memorialized to seize Tiao; he was imprisoned and executed; he was thirty-six.

sentences.zh: 臨終謂門賓曰：「寄語沈公，君方為三代史，亦不得見沒。」

translations.literal: Facing death he told gate guests, "Tell Master Shen: you are about to write history for three dynasties—you must not let me be erased.
translations.idiomatic: At the point of death he told gate guests, "Tell Master Shen: you are about to write history for three dynasties—you must not let me be erased.

sentences.zh: 初，朓告王敬則反，敬則女為朓妻，常懷刀欲報朓，朓不敢相見。

translations.literal: Earlier when Tiao reported Wang Jingze's rebellion, Jingze's daughter was Tiao's wife and always kept a knife wanting to avenge Tiao; Tiao did not dare meet her.
translations.idiomatic: Before this, when Tiao reported Wang Jingze's rebellion, Jingze's daughter was Tiao's wife and always kept a knife wanting to avenge Tiao; Tiao did not dare meet her.

sentences.zh: 及當拜吏部，謙挹尤甚，尚書郎范縝嘲之曰：「卿人才無慚小選，但恨不可刑于寡妻。

translations.literal: When he was about to be appointed to the Ministry of Personnel his modesty was especially deep; Gentleman of the Masters of Writing Fan Zhen mocked him, "Your talent is nothing to shame a small selection—but alas, you cannot discipline your few wife.
translations.idiomatic: When he was about to be appointed to the Ministry of Personnel his modesty was especially deep; Gentleman Fan Zhen mocked him, "Your talent is nothing to shame a small selection—but alas, you cannot discipline your few wife.

sentences.zh: 」朓有愧色。

translations.literal: Tiao had a shamefaced look.
translations.idiomatic: Tiao flushed with shame.

sentences.zh: 及臨誅，歎曰：「天道其不可昧乎！

translations.literal: Facing execution he sighed, "Heaven's way—can it be obscured?
translations.idiomatic: "Heaven's way—can it be obscured?, facing execution he sighed

sentences.zh: 我雖不殺王公，王公因我而死。」

translations.literal: Though I did not kill Lord Wang, Lord Wang died because of me.
translations.idiomatic: Although I did not kill Lord Wang, Lord Wang died because of me.

sentences.zh: 朓好獎人才，會稽孔覬粗有才筆，未為時知，孔珪嘗令草讓表以示朓。

translations.literal: Tiao loved to reward talent; Kuaiji's Kong Xian had rough talent with the brush and was not yet known to the age; Kong Gui once had him draft a decline memorial to show Tiao.
translations.idiomatic: Tiao loved to reward talent; Kuaiji's Kong Xian had rough talent with the brush and was not yet known; Kong Gui once had him draft a decline memorial to show Tiao.

sentences.zh: 朓嗟吟良久，手自折簡寫之，謂珪曰：「士子聲名未立，應共獎成，無惜齒牙餘論。

translations.literal: Tiao chanted long and personally folded bamboo and wrote it out, telling Gui, "When a gentleman's fame is not yet established, we should together help him succeed—do not spare the leftover talk of teeth.
translations.idiomatic: Tiao chanted long and personally folded bamboo and wrote it out, telling Gui, "When a gentleman's fame is not yet established, we should together help him succeed—do not spare the leftover talk of teeth."

sentences.zh: 」其好善如此。

translations.literal: His love of good was like this.
translations.idiomatic: His love of good became like this.

sentences.zh: 朓及殷叡素與梁武以文章相得，帝以大女永興公主適叡子鈞，第二女永世公主適朓子謨。

translations.literal: Tiao and Yin Rui from of old were joined with Emperor Wu of Liang through literature; the Emperor gave his eldest daughter Princess Yongxing to Rui's son Jun and his second daughter Princess Yongshi to Tiao's son Mo.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor gave his eldest daughter Princess Yongxing to Rui's son Jun and his second daughter Princess Yongshi to Tiao's son Mo.; tiao and Yin Rui from of old were joined with Emperor Wu of Liang through literature

sentences.zh: 及帝為雍州，二女並暫隨母向州。

translations.literal: When the Emperor was Governor of Yong Province, both daughters temporarily followed their mother to the province.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor became Governor of Yong Province, both daughters temporarily followed their mother to the province.

sentences.zh: 及武帝即位，二主始隨內還。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu took the throne, both princesses then followed inside and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu took the throne, both princesses then returned to court.

sentences.zh: 武帝意薄謨，又以門單，欲更適張弘策子，弘策卒，又以與王志子諲。

translations.literal: The Emperor's regard for Mo was thin, and because the gate was single he wished to remarry her to Zhang Hongce's son; when Hongce died, he again gave her to Wang Zhi's son Yin.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's regard for Mo was thin, and because the gate was single he wished to remarry her to Zhang Hongce's son; when Hongce died, he again gave her to Wang Zhi's son Yin.

sentences.zh: 而謨不堪歎恨，為書狀如詩贈主。

translations.literal: Mo could not bear the sigh of regret and wrote a letter in prose like poetry to give the princess.
translations.idiomatic: Mo could not bear the sigh of regret and wrote a letter in prose like poetry to the princess.

sentences.zh: 主以呈帝，甚蒙矜歎，而婦終不得還。

translations.literal: The princess presented it to the Emperor; he greatly pitied and praised it, yet the wife never returned.
translations.idiomatic: That princess presented it to the Emperor; he greatly pitied and praised it, yet the wife never returned.

sentences.zh: 尋用謨為信安縣，稍遷王府諮議。

translations.literal: Soon Mo was used as Magistrate of Xin'an County, then gradually promoted to Staff Officer to the Prince's establishment.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Mo was made Magistrate of Xin'an County, then gradually promoted to Staff Officer to the Prince's establishment.

sentences.zh: 時以為沈約早與朓善，為制此書云。

translations.literal: At the time people thought Shen Yue early befriended Tiao and composed this letter.
translations.idiomatic: Then people thought Shen Yue early befriended Tiao and composed this letter.

sentences.zh: 從祖弟 方明

translations.literal: Father's younger cousin's younger brother Fangming
translations.idiomatic: The father's younger cousin's younger brother, Fangming

sentences.zh: 謝方明，裕從祖弟也。

translations.literal: Xie Fangming was Yu's father's younger cousin's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Fangming became Yu's father's younger cousin's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 祖鐵字鐵石，位永嘉太守。

translations.literal: Grandfather Tie, styled Tieshi, held the post of Administrator of Yongjia.
translations.idiomatic: Grandfather Tie, styled Tieshi, served as Administrator of Yongjia.

sentences.zh: 父沖字秀度，中書郎，家在會稽，病歸，為孫恩所殺，贈散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Father Chong, styled Xiudu, was Gentleman of the Secretariat; his family was in Kuaiji; he returned home ill and was killed by Sun En; posthumously titled Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Father Chong, courtesy name Xiudu, was Gentleman of the Secretariat; his family was in Kuaiji; he returned home ill and was killed by Sun En; posthumously titled Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 方明隨伯父吳興太守邈在郡。

translations.literal: Fangming followed his uncle, Administrator of Wuxing Miao, in the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Fangming followed his uncle Wuxing Administrator Miao in the commandery.

sentences.zh: 孫恩寇會稽，東土諸郡回應，吳興人胡桀、郜驃破東遷縣，方明勸邈避之，不從，賊至被害，方明逃免。

translations.literal: Sun En raided Kuaiji; the eastern commanderies responded; Wu men Hu Jie and Gao Biao broke Dongqian County; Fangming urged Miao to avoid them but he would not listen; when bandits arrived Miao was killed and Fangming escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Sun En raided Kuaiji; the eastern commanderies responded; Wu men Hu Jie and Gao Biao broke Dongqian County; Fangming urged Miao to avoid them but he would not listen; when bandits arrived Miao became killed and Fangming escaped.

sentences.zh: 初，邈舅子長樂馮嗣之及北方學士馮翊仇玄達俱投邈，禮待甚簡，二人並恨，遂與恩通謀。

translations.literal: Earlier, Miao's sister's son Feng Sizhi of Changle and northern scholar Qiu Xuanda of Fufeng both came to Miao; they were treated with very simple courtesy and both resented it; they then conspired with En.
translations.idiomatic: Before this, Miao's sister's son Feng Sizhi of Changle and northern scholar Qiu Xuanda of Fufeng both came to Miao; they were treated with very simple courtesy and both resented it; they then conspired with En.

sentences.zh: 劉牢之、謝琰等討恩，恩走臨海，嗣之等不得同去，方更聚合。

translations.literal: Liu Laozhi and Xie Yan and others attacked En; En fled to Linhai; Sizhi and the others could not go along and gathered again.
translations.idiomatic: En fled to Linhai; liu Laozhi and Xie Yan and others attacked En

sentences.zh: 方明體素羸弱，而勇決過人，結邈門生討嗣之等，悉禽手刃之。

translations.literal: Fangming's body was always frail and weak, yet his courage and decisiveness surpassed others; he gathered Miao's gate students to attack Sizhi and the others and captured them all, personally beheading them.
translations.idiomatic: Fangming's body became always frail and weak, yet his courage and decisiveness surpassed others; he gathered Miao's gate students to attack Sizhi and the others and captured them all, personally beheading them.

sentences.zh: 時亂後吉凶禮廢，方明合門遇禍，資產無遺，而營舉凶功盡力，數月葬送並畢，平世備禮無以加也。

translations.literal: At the time after the chaos the rites of fortune and mourning were abandoned; Fangming's whole gate met disaster and not an asset remained, yet he managed funeral work with all his strength; within months burial and sending-off were complete—peaceful-age full rites could not surpass it.
translations.idiomatic: Then after the chaos the rites of fortune and mourning were abandoned; Fangming's whole gate met disaster and not an asset remained, yet he managed funeral work with all his strength; within months burial and sending-off were complete—peaceful-age full rites could not surpass it.

sentences.zh: 頃之，孫恩重陷會稽，謝琰見害，因購方明甚急。

translations.literal: Soon Sun En again took Kuaiji; Xie Yan was killed; En therefore put a high price on Fangming's head.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, Sun En again took Kuaiji; Xie Yan was killed; En therefore put a high price on Fangming's head.

sentences.zh: 方明于上虞載母妹奔東陽，由黃櫱嶠出鄱陽，附載還都，寄居國子學。

translations.literal: Fangming at Shangyu loaded his mother and younger sister and fled to Dongyang; by Huangbo Ridge he came out to Poyang, took passage and returned to the capital, and lodged at the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: At Shangyu Fangming loaded his mother and younger sister and fled to Dongyang; by Huangbo Ridge he came out to Poyang, took passage back to the capital, and lodged at the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 流離險厄，屯苦備經，而貞履之操，在約無改。

translations.literal: Wandering through peril and hardship, he endured every kind of trial, yet his steadfast conduct in straitened circumstances never changed.
translations.idiomatic: Wandering through peril and hardship, he endured every kind of trial, yet his steadfast conduct in straitened circumstances never wavered.

sentences.zh: 桓玄克建鄴，丹陽尹卞範之勢傾朝野，欲以女嫁方明，方明終不回。

translations.literal: When Huan Xuan took Jiankang, Acting Governor of Danyang Bian Fanzhi's power tilted court and countryside; he wished to marry his daughter to Fangming but Fangming never yielded.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Xuan took Jiankang, Acting Danyang Governor Bian Fanzhi's power tilted court and countryside; he wished to marry his daughter to Fangming but Fangming never yielded.

sentences.zh: 桓玄聞而賞之，即除著作佐郎。

translations.literal: Huan Xuan heard and praised this; he was at once made Assistant Editor in the Editorial Office.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan heard and praised this; he became at once made Assistant Editor in the Editorial Office.

sentences.zh: 後從兄景仁舉為宋武中軍主簿，方明知無不為，帝謂曰：「愧未有瓜衍之賞，且當與卿共豫章國祿。

translations.literal: Later his elder cousin Jingren recommended him as Chief Clerk to Emperor Wu's Central Army; Fangming in knowing did nothing not done; the Emperor said, "I am ashamed not to have a Guayan reward—yet I will share with you the revenue of Yuzhang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Later his elder cousin Jingren recommended him as Chief Clerk to Emperor Wu's Central Army; Fangming left nothing undone in what he knew; the Emperor said, "I am ashamed not to have a Guayan reward—yet I will share with you the revenue of Yuzhang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 」屢加賞賜。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly given rewards.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly rewarded.

sentences.zh: 方明嚴恪，善自居遇，雖暗室未嘗有惰容。

translations.literal: Fangming was stern and strict, good at conducting himself; even in a dark room he never had a lazy face.
translations.idiomatic: Fangming became stern and strict, good at conducting himself; even in a dark room he never had a lazy face.

sentences.zh: 從兄混有重名，唯歲節朝拜而已。

translations.literal: His elder cousin Hun had heavy fame; he only paid New Year and festival respects.
translations.idiomatic: His elder cousin Hun had heavy fame; Fangming only paid New Year and festival respects.

sentences.zh: 丹陽尹劉穆之權重當時，朝野輻湊，其不至者唯混、方明、郗僧施、蔡廓四人而已。

translations.literal: Acting Governor of Danyang Liu Muzhi's power weighed on the age; court and countryside thronged—those who did not come were only Hun, Fangming, Xi Sengshi, and Cai Kuo.
translations.idiomatic: Acting Danyang Governor Liu Muzhi's power weighed on the age; court and countryside thronged—those who did not come were only Hun, Fangming, Xi Sengshi, and Cai Kuo.

sentences.zh: 穆之甚恨。

translations.literal: Muzhi greatly resented this.
translations.idiomatic: Muzhi resented this deeply.

sentences.zh: 及混等誅後，方明、廓來往造穆之，穆之大悅，白武帝曰：「謝方明可謂名家駒，及蔡廓直置並台鼎人，無論復有才用。

translations.literal: When Hun and the others were executed, Fangming and Kuo came to visit Muzhi; Muzhi was greatly pleased and told Emperor Wu, "Xie Fangming can be called a colt of a famous house, and Cai Kuo straight placed are both tower-and-tripod men, to say nothing of further talent.
translations.idiomatic: When Hun and the others were executed, Fangming and Kuo came to visit Muzhi; Muzhi became greatly pleased and told Emperor Wu, "Xie Fangming can be called a colt of a famous house, and Cai Kuo straight placed are both tower-and-tripod men, to say nothing of further talent.

sentences.zh: 」頃之，轉從事中郎，仍為左將軍道憐長史，武帝令府中眾事皆諮決之。

translations.literal: Soon he transferred to Attendant Gentleman and was again Chief Clerk to the Left General Daolian, and the Emperor ordered that all headquarters affairs be referred to him for decision.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, he transferred to Attendant Gentleman and was again Chief Clerk to the Left General Daolian, and the Emperor ordered that all headquarters affairs be referred to him for decision.

sentences.zh: 府轉為中軍長史，尋加晉陵太守，復為驃騎長史、南郡相，委任如初。

translations.literal: The headquarters became Central Army Chief Clerk; soon he was also Administrator of Jinling, then again Chief Clerk to the Cavalry General and Chancellor of Nan Commandery, entrusted as before.
translations.idiomatic: That headquarters became Central Army Chief Clerk; soon he was also Administrator of Jinling, then again Chief Clerk to the Cavalry General and Chancellor of Nan Commandery, entrusted as before.

sentences.zh: 嘗年終，江陵縣獄囚事無輕重，悉放歸家，使過正三日還到，罪重者二十餘人，綱紀以下莫不疑懼。

translations.literal: Once at year's end he released all prisoners of Jiangling County regardless of gravity of offense to return home, to come back after the first month for three days; more than twenty had heavy crimes; clerks below the warden all doubted and feared.
translations.idiomatic: Once at year's end he released all Jiangling County prisoners regardless of offense gravity to return home, to come back after the first month for three days; more than twenty had heavy crimes; clerks below the warden all doubted and feared.

sentences.zh: 時晉陵郡送故主簿弘季咸、徐壽之並隨在西，固諫，以為昔人雖有其事，或是記籍過言，且當今人情偽薄，不可以古義相許。

translations.literal: At the time Jinling Commandery sent former Chief Clerk Hong Jixian and Xu Shouzhi, who followed in the west, and they firmly remonstrated, saying though men of old had such a thing, it might be excessive words in records; moreover present human feeling is false and thin—it cannot be promised on ancient meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Then Jinling Commandery sent former Chief Clerk Hong Jixian and Xu Shouzhi, who followed in the west, and they firmly remonstrated, saying though men of old had such a thing, it might be excessive words in records; moreover present human feeling is false and thin—it cannot be promised on ancient meaning.

sentences.zh: 方明不納，一時遣之。

translations.literal: Fangming did not accept and sent them all off at once.
translations.idiomatic: Fangming would not hear of it and sent them all home at once.

sentences.zh: 囚及父兄並驚喜涕泣，以為就死無恨。

translations.literal: Prisoners and fathers and elder brothers all wept in surprise and joy, thinking to die without regret.
translations.idiomatic: Prisoners and fathers and elder brothers wept in surprise and joy, thinking to die without regret.

sentences.zh: 至期有重罪一人醉不能歸，違二日乃反。

translations.literal: When the term came one with heavy crime was drunk and could not return; he was two days late before he came back.
translations.idiomatic: When the term came one with heavy crime became drunk and could not return; he was two days late before he came back.

sentences.zh: 餘一囚十日不來，五官朱幹期請見，欲自討之。

translations.literal: One other prisoner did not come for ten days; Fifth Officer Zhu Ganqi asked to see him, wanting to punish himself.
translations.idiomatic: One other prisoner did not return for ten days; Fifth Officer Zhu Ganqi asked to see Fangming, wanting to punish himself.

sentences.zh: 方明知為囚事，使左右謝五官不須入，囚自當反。

translations.literal: Fangming knew it was a prisoner matter and had attendants tell the Fifth Officer not to enter—the prisoner would return on his own.
translations.idiomatic: Fangming knew it became a prisoner matter and had attendants tell the Fifth Officer not to enter—the prisoner would return on his own.

sentences.zh: 囚逡巡墟裏，不能自歸，鄉村責讓率領將送，竟無逃者。

translations.literal: The prisoner wandered in the hamlet and could not bring himself to return; village people reproached and led him to deliver him—there were none who fled.
translations.idiomatic: That prisoner wandered in the hamlet and could not bring himself to return; village people reproached and led him to deliver him—there were none who fled.

sentences.zh: 遠近嘆服焉。

translations.literal: Near and far sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: People near and far sighed in admiration.

sentences.zh: 宋武帝受命，位侍中，丹陽尹，有能名。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Song received Heaven's mandate, Fangming held Palace Attendant and Acting Governor of Danyang and had a reputation for capacity.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu received Heaven's mandate, Fangming held Palace Attendant and Acting Governor of Danyang and had a reputation for capacity.

sentences.zh: 轉會稽太守。

translations.literal: He transferred to Administrator of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: He moved on to Administrator of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 江東人戶殷盛，風俗峻刻，強弱相陵，奸吏蜂起，符書一下，文攝相續。

translations.literal: East of the river households were abundant and prosperous; customs were harsh and cutting; strong oppressed weak; corrupt clerks swarmed; when a warrant came down, documents of seizure followed in succession.
translations.idiomatic: East of the river households were abundant; customs were harsh and cutting; strong oppressed weak; corrupt clerks swarmed; when a warrant came down, documents of seizure followed in succession.

sentences.zh: 方明深達政體，不拘文法，闊略苛細，務在統領。

translations.literal: Fangming deeply understood the body of governance; he was not bound by written law, broadly passed over harsh minutiae, and aimed at overall command.
translations.idiomatic: Fangming deeply understood the body of governance; he became not bound by written law, broadly passed over harsh minutiae, and aimed at overall command.

sentences.zh: 貴族豪士，莫敢犯禁。

translations.literal: Nobles and powerful men did not dare violate prohibition.
translations.idiomatic: Nobles and powerful families did not dare break the law.

sentences.zh: 除比伍之坐，判久系之獄。

translations.literal: He removed collective punishment of neighbors and judged long-imprisoned cases.
translations.idiomatic: This man removed collective punishment of neighbors and judged long-imprisoned cases.

sentences.zh: 前後征伐，每兵運不充，悉倩士庶，事寧皆使還本。

translations.literal: In repeated campaigns whenever military transport was insufficient he borrowed gentry and commoners; when affairs ended he always sent them back to their origins.
translations.idiomatic: In repeated campaigns whenever military transport became insufficient he borrowed gentry and commoners; when affairs ended he always sent them back to their origins.

sentences.zh: 而守宰不明，與奪乖謬，人事不至，必被抑塞。

translations.literal: Yet the guarding administrators were not clear and their grants and withholdings went awry; human affairs did not reach and one was sure to be blocked.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the guarding administrators were not clear and their grants and withholdings went awry; human affairs did not reach and one became sure to be blocked.

sentences.zh: 方明簡汰精當，各順所宜，東土稱詠之。

translations.literal: Fangming sifted and chose with precision; each followed what was fitting; the eastern lands praised and chanted this.
translations.idiomatic: Fangming sifted and chose with precision; each followed what became fitting; the eastern lands praised and chanted this.

sentences.zh: 性尤愛惜人物，未嘗有所是非。

translations.literal: His nature especially cherished people; he never had right or wrong toward anyone.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he especially cherished people; he never had right or wrong toward anyone.

sentences.zh: 承代前人，不易其政；

translations.literal: He succeeded predecessors and did not change their policies;
translations.idiomatic: This man succeeded predecessors and did not change their policies;

sentences.zh: 必宜改者，則漸變使無跡可尋。

translations.literal: where change was necessary he gradually altered so no trace could be found.
translations.idiomatic: where change became necessary he gradually altered so no trace could be found.

sentences.zh: 卒官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 子 惠連

translations.literal: Son Huilian
translations.idiomatic: The son, Huilian

sentences.zh: 子惠連，年十歲能屬文，族兄靈運嘉賞之，云：「每有篇章，對惠連輒得佳語」。

translations.literal: His son Huilian at ten could compose prose; clansman elder brother Lingyun praised and prized him, saying, "Whenever I have a piece, facing Huilian I always get a fine line.
translations.idiomatic: His son Huilian at ten could compose prose; clansman elder brother Lingyun praised him, saying, "Whenever I have a piece, facing Huilian I always get a fine line.

sentences.zh: 嘗於永嘉西堂思詩，竟日不就，忽夢見惠連，即得「池塘生春草」，大以為工。

translations.literal: Once at Yongjia's Western Hall he was thinking on a poem; all day he did not finish; suddenly he dreamed of Huilian and at once obtained "Pond bank births spring grass"; he greatly thought it skilled.
translations.idiomatic: Once at Yongjia's Western Hall he became thinking on a poem; all day he did not finish; suddenly he dreamed of Huilian and at once obtained "Pond bank births spring grass"; he greatly thought it skilled.

sentences.zh: 常云：「此語有神功，非吾語也」。

translations.literal: He often said, "This line has divine power—it is not my words.
translations.idiomatic: This man often said, "This line has divine power—it is not my words.

sentences.zh: 本州辟主簿，不就。

translations.literal: The province summoned him as Chief Clerk; he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: That province summoned him as Chief Clerk; he did not accept.

sentences.zh: 惠連先愛幸會稽郡吏杜德靈，及居父憂，贈以五言詩十餘首，「乘流遵歸路。

translations.literal: Huilian first loved and was favored by Kuaiji Commandery clerk Du Deling; when in mourning for his father he gave him more than ten pentasyllabic poems, "Following the current, keeping to the homeward road.
translations.idiomatic: Huilian first loved and became favored by Kuaiji Commandery clerk Du Deling; when in mourning for his father he gave him more than ten pentasyllabic poems, "Following the current, keeping to the homeward road.

sentences.zh: 」諸篇是也。

translations.literal: Such were the pieces.
translations.idiomatic: Those were the pieces.

sentences.zh: 坐廢不豫榮位。

translations.literal: For this he was disgraced and did not participate in honored rank.
translations.idiomatic: For this he became disgraced and did not participate in honored rank.

sentences.zh: 尚書僕射殷景仁愛其才，言次白文帝，言：「臣小兒時便見此文，而論者雲是惠連，其實非也」。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Yin Jingren loved his talent and in conversation told Emperor Wen, saying, "In my small childhood I already saw this writing, and debaters said it was Huilian's—it was actually not.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Yin Jingren loved his talent and in conversation told Emperor Wen, "In my small childhood I already saw this writing, and debaters said it was Huilian's—it was actually not.

sentences.zh: 文帝曰：「若此便應通之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen said, "If so, he should be cleared.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen said, "If that is so, he should be cleared."

sentences.zh: 」元嘉七年，方為司徒彭城王義康法曹行參軍。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Yuanjia he was made Army Registrar on Prince Yikang of Pengcheng's Law Office staff.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia year seven he was made Army Registrar on Prince Yikang of Pengcheng's Law Office staff.

sentences.zh: 義康修東府城，城塹中得古塚，為之改葬，使惠連為祭文，留信待成，其文甚美。

translations.literal: Yikang repaired the Eastern Headquarters city wall; in the moat an ancient tomb was found; he had it reburied and had Huilian compose the sacrificial text; he kept a messenger waiting for it to be finished—the text was very beautiful.
translations.idiomatic: Yikang repaired the Eastern Headquarters city wall; in the moat an ancient tomb became found; he had it reburied and had Huilian compose the sacrificial text; he kept a messenger waiting for it to be finished—the text was very beautiful.

sentences.zh: 又為雪賦，以高麗見奇。

translations.literal: He also composed "Rhapsody on Snow," noted for its loftiness and beauty.
translations.idiomatic: He likewise composed "Rhapsody on Snow," noted for its loftiness and beauty.

sentences.zh: 靈運見其新文，每曰：「張華重生，不能易也「。

translations.literal: Lingyun seeing his new writing always said, "If Zhang Hua were reborn, he could not change it.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Huilian's new writing, Lingyun always said, "If Zhang Hua were reborn, he could not change a word."

sentences.zh: 文章並行於世，年三十七卒。

translations.literal: His writings circulated together in the world; he died at thirty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died at thirty-seven.; his writings circulated together in the world

sentences.zh: 既早亡，輕薄多尤累，故官不顯。

translations.literal: Having died young, with many frivolous faults and encumbrances, his office was not conspicuous.
translations.idiomatic: Having died young, with many frivolous faults and encumbrances, his office became not conspicuous.

sentences.zh: 無子。

translations.literal: He had no son.
translations.idiomatic: He had no son.

sentences.zh: 惠連弟惠宣，位臨川太守。

translations.literal: Huilian's younger brother Huixuan held the post of Administrator of Linchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Huilian's younger brother Huixuan served as Administrator of Linchuan.

sentences.zh: 謝靈運

translations.literal: Xie Lingyun
translations.idiomatic: Xie Lingyun

sentences.zh: 謝靈運，安西將軍弈之曾孫而方明從子也。

translations.literal: Xie Lingyun was great-grandson of General Who Pacifies the West Yi and Fangming's father's younger cousin's son.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Lingyun became great-grandson of General Who Pacifies the West Yi and Fangming's father's younger cousin's son.

sentences.zh: 祖玄，晉車騎將軍。

translations.literal: Grandfather Xuan was Cavalry General under Jin.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xuan served as Cavalry General under Jin.

sentences.zh: 父瑍，生而不慧，位秘書郎，早亡。

translations.literal: Father Min was dull from birth, held the post of Secretary Lang, and died young.
translations.idiomatic: Father Min was dull from birth, served as Secretary Lang, and died young.

sentences.zh: 靈運幼便穎悟，玄甚異之。

translations.literal: Lingyun from youth was sharp and understanding; Xuan greatly marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: Lingyun from childhood was sharp and understanding; Xuan greatly marveled at him.

sentences.zh: 謂親知曰：「我乃生瑍，瑍兒何為不及我。」

translations.literal: He told kin and friends, "I produced Min; how is Min's son not my equal?
translations.idiomatic: He told kin and friends, "I produced Min—how is Min's son not my equal?

sentences.zh: 靈運少好學，博覽群書，文章之美，與顏延之為江左第一。

translations.literal: Lingyun from youth loved learning, ranged through many books; the beauty of his writing, with Yan Yanzhi, was first in the Jiangzuo region.
translations.idiomatic: Lingyun from childhood loved learning, ranged through many books; the beauty of his writing, with Yan Yanzhi, was first in the Jiangzuo region.

sentences.zh: 縱橫俊發過於延之，深密則不如也。

translations.literal: In horizontal sweep and brilliant outpouring he surpassed Yanzhi; in depth and density he did not match.
translations.idiomatic: In depth and density he did not match.; in horizontal sweep and brilliant outpouring he surpassed Yanzhi

sentences.zh: 從叔混特知愛之。

translations.literal: His father's younger cousin Hun especially knew and loved him.
translations.idiomatic: His father's younger cousin Hun took special knowledge and love of him.

sentences.zh: 襲封康樂公，以國公例除員外散騎侍郎，不就。

translations.literal: He inherited enfeoffment as Duke of Kangle; by the precedent for a state duke he was appointed Extraordinary Gentleman of Scattered Cavalry but did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: This man inherited enfeoffment as Duke of Kangle; by the precedent for a state duke he was appointed Extraordinary Gentleman of Scattered Cavalry but did not accept.

sentences.zh: 為琅邪王大司馬行參軍。

translations.literal: He was Army Registrar on the Grand Marshal staff of the Prince of Langye.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Army Registrar on the Grand Marshal staff of the Prince of Langye.

sentences.zh: 性豪侈，車服鮮麗，衣物多改舊形制，世共宗之，咸稱謝康樂也。

translations.literal: His nature was extravagant; carriage and dress were fresh and gorgeous; clothing often changed old forms; the world together took him as model and all called him Xie Kangle.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was extravagant; carriage and dress were fresh and gorgeous; clothing often changed old forms; the world together took him as model and all called him Xie Kangle.

sentences.zh: 累遷秘書丞，坐事免。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Secretary Director and was dismissed for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Secretary Director and was dismissed for an offense.

sentences.zh: 宋武帝在長安，靈運為世子中軍諮議、黃門侍郎，奉使慰勞武帝于彭城，作撰征賦。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Song was at Chang'an, Lingyun was Staff Officer to the Heir Apparent's Central Army and Gentleman of the Yellow Gate; he was sent as envoy to comfort Emperor Wu at Pengcheng and composed "Rhapsody on Composing the Expedition.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Song became at Chang'an, Lingyun was Staff Officer to the Heir Apparent's Central Army and Gentleman of the Yellow Gate; he was sent as envoy to comfort Emperor Wu at Pengcheng and composed "Rhapsody on Composing the Expedition.

sentences.zh: 後為相國從事中郎，世子左衛率，坐輒殺門生免官。

translations.literal: Later he was Attendant Gentleman on the Chancellor's staff, Left Commandant of the Heir Apparent's Guard, and was dismissed from office for summarily killing a gate student.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was Attendant Gentleman on the Chancellor's staff and Left Commandant of the Heir Apparent's Guard, then dismissed for summarily killing a gate student.

sentences.zh: 宋受命，降公爵為侯，又為太子左衛率。

translations.literal: When Song received Heaven's mandate, his ducal rank was reduced to marquis; he was again Left Commandant of the Heir Apparent's Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Song received Heaven's mandate, his ducal rank became reduced to marquis; he was again Left Commandant of the Heir Apparent's Guard.

sentences.zh: 靈運多愆禮度，朝廷唯以文義處之，不以應實相許。

translations.literal: Lingyun often transgressed ritual measure; the court only treated him for literary meaning and did not promise him real office.
translations.idiomatic: Lingyun often transgressed ritual measure; the court only treated him for literary gifts and did not promise him real office.

sentences.zh: 自謂才能宜參權要，既不見知，常懷憤惋。

translations.literal: He himself thought his talent should share in power; not being recognized, he always harbored anger and resentment.
translations.idiomatic: This man himself thought his talent should share in power; not being recognized, he always harbored anger and resentment.

sentences.zh: 廬陵王義真少好文籍，與靈運情款異常。

translations.literal: Prince Yizhen of Luling from youth loved literature and had exceptional intimacy with Lingyun.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yizhen of Luling from youth loved literature and was exceptionally close to Lingyun.

sentences.zh: 少帝即位，權在大臣，靈運構扇異同，非毀執政，司徒徐羨之等患之，出為永嘉太守。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shao took the throne, power lay with great ministers; Lingyun stirred differences and slandered those in power; Minister of Education Xu Xianzhi and others were troubled and sent him out as Administrator of Yongjia.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shao took the throne, power lay with great ministers; Lingyun stirred faction and slandered those in power; Minister of Education Xu Xianzhi and others were troubled and sent him out as Administrator of Yongjia.

sentences.zh: 郡有名山水，靈運素所愛好。

translations.literal: The commandery had famous mountains and waters that Lingyun had always loved.
translations.idiomatic: That commandery had famous mountains and waters that Lingyun had always loved.

sentences.zh: 出守既不得志，遂肆意遊遨，遍曆諸縣，動踰旬朔。

translations.literal: Going out to govern and not attaining his aim, he then roamed at will, traversing every county, often moving for more than ten days or a month.
translations.idiomatic: Denied the aims he sought in office, he roamed at will, traversing every county, often absent for ten days or a month at a time.

sentences.zh: 理人聽訟，不復關懷，所至輒為詩詠以致其意。

translations.literal: Governing people and hearing lawsuits he no longer cared; wherever he went he composed poetry to express his intent.
translations.idiomatic: Governing people and hearing lawsuits no longer held him; wherever he went he composed poetry to express his intent.

sentences.zh: 在郡一周，稱疾去職，從弟晦、曜、弘微等並與書止之，不從。

translations.literal: After one year in the commandery he claimed illness and left office; younger cousins Hui, Yao, Hongwei, and others all wrote to stop him; he did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: After one year in the commandery he claimed illness and left office; younger cousins Hui, Yao, Hongwei, and others all wrote to stop him; he would not listen.

sentences.zh: 靈運父祖並葬始寧縣，並有故宅及墅，遂移籍會稽，修營舊業。

translations.literal: Lingyun's father and grandfather were both buried in Shining County and there were old residences and villas; he then moved his registration to Kuaiji and repaired the old estate.
translations.idiomatic: Lingyun's father and grandfather were both buried in Shining County and there were old residences and villas; he moved his registration to Kuaiji and repaired the old estate.

sentences.zh: 傍山帶江，盡幽居之美。

translations.literal: Beside mountains and embracing rivers, he had the utmost beauty of secluded dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: Beside mountains and embracing rivers, he possessed the utmost beauty of secluded dwelling.

sentences.zh: 與隱士王弘之、孔淳之等放蕩為娛，有終焉之志。

translations.literal: With recluses Wang Hongzhi, Kong Chunzhi, and others he roamed freely for pleasure and had the will to end his days there.
translations.idiomatic: With recluses Wang Hongzhi, Kong Chunzhi, and others he roamed freely for pleasure and meant to end his days there.

sentences.zh: 每有一首詩至都下，貴賤莫不競寫，宿昔間士庶皆遍，名動都下。

translations.literal: Whenever he had one poem reach the capital, noble and base all competed to copy it; within a night gentry and commoners all had it—his name shook the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever a poem reached the capital, noble and base all competed to copy it; within a night gentry and commoners all had it—his name shook the capital.

sentences.zh: 作山居賦，並自注以言其事。

translations.literal: He composed "Rhapsody on Mountain Dwelling" and himself annotated it to tell its affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He composed "Rhapsody on Mountain Dwelling" and annotated it himself to tell its affairs.

sentences.zh: 文帝誅徐羨之等，徵為秘書監，再召不起。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen executed Xu Xianzhi and the others, Lingyun was summoned as Director of the Secretariat; twice summoned he did not rise.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen executed Xu Xianzhi and the others, Lingyun became summoned as Director of the Secretariat; twice summoned he did not rise.

sentences.zh: 使光祿大夫范泰與書敦獎，乃出。

translations.literal: Grand Master of Splendid Happiness Fan Tai was sent with a letter to urge and reward him; then he came out.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Master of Splendid Happiness Fan Tai became sent with a letter to urge and reward him; then he came out.

sentences.zh: 使整秘閣書遺闕，又令撰晉書，粗立條流，書竟不就。

translations.literal: He was ordered to put in order the Secretariat's missing books and also to compile the History of Jin; he roughly set the categories and flow but the book was not completed.
translations.idiomatic: This man was ordered to put in order the Secretariat's missing books and also to compile the History of Jin; he roughly set the categories and flow but the book was not completed.

sentences.zh: 尋遷侍中，賞遇甚厚。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Palace Attendant and favored very generously.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, he was transferred to Palace Attendant and favored very generously.

sentences.zh: 靈運詩書皆兼獨絕，每文竟，手自寫之，文帝稱為二寶。

translations.literal: Lingyun's poetry and calligraphy were both uniquely supreme; whenever a piece was finished he personally wrote it out; Emperor Wen called them two treasures.
translations.idiomatic: Lingyun's poetry and calligraphy were both uniquely supreme; whenever a piece became finished he personally wrote it out; Emperor Wen called them two treasures.

sentences.zh: 既自以名輩，應參時政，至是唯以文義見接，每侍上宴，談賞而已。

translations.literal: He himself thought that by fame and generation he should share in current governance; now he was only received for literary meaning; whenever he attended the Emperor at banquets it was talk and praise only.
translations.idiomatic: This man himself thought that by fame and generation he should share in current governance; now he was only received for literary meaning; whenever he attended the Emperor at banquets it was talk and praise only.

sentences.zh: 王曇首、王華、殷景仁等名位素不踰之，並見任遇，意既不平，多稱疾不朝直。

translations.literal: Wang Tan Shou, Wang Hua, Yin Jingren, and others in name and rank had never surpassed him yet all received trust and favor; his intent was not equal and he often claimed illness and did not attend regular court.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tan Shou, Wang Hua, Yin Jingren, and others in name and rank had never surpassed him yet all received trust and favor; his intent became not equal and he often claimed illness and did not attend regular court.

sentences.zh: 穿池植援，種竹樹果，驅課公役，無復期度。

translations.literal: He dug pools and planted screens, planted bamboo, trees, and fruit, and drove corvée labor without any schedule.
translations.idiomatic: He dug pools and planted screens, bamboo, trees, and fruit, and drove corvée labor without any schedule.

sentences.zh: 出郭遊行，或一百六七十里，經旬不歸。

translations.literal: Going outside the city to roam, sometimes one hundred sixty or seventy li; for ten days or more he did not return.
translations.idiomatic: Roaming outside the city, sometimes one hundred sixty or seventy li; for ten days or more he did not return.

sentences.zh: 既無表聞，又不請急。

translations.literal: He had neither memorial to inform nor request for urgent leave.
translations.idiomatic: He neither memorialized nor requested urgent leave.

sentences.zh: 上不欲傷大臣，諷旨令自解。

translations.literal: The Emperor did not wish to harm a great minister and hinted that he should resign himself.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not wish to harm a great minister and hinted that he should resign himself.

sentences.zh: 靈運表陳疾，賜假東歸。

translations.literal: Lingyun memorialized stating illness and was granted leave to return east.
translations.idiomatic: Lingyun memorialized stating illness and became granted leave to return east.

sentences.zh: 將行，上書勸伐河北。

translations.literal: About to leave, he submitted a memorial urging campaign against north of the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: About to leave, he submitted a memorial urging a campaign north of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 而遊娛宴集，以夜續晝。

translations.literal: Yet he roamed and feasted, continuing day from night.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he still roamed and feasted, carrying day on into night.

sentences.zh: 復為御史中丞傅隆奏免官，是歲，元嘉五年也。

translations.literal: Again Censor-in-Chief Fu Long memorialized to dismiss him from office; that year was the fifth year of Yuanjia.
translations.idiomatic: Again Censor-in-Chief Fu Long memorialized to dismiss him from office; that year became the fifth year of Yuanjia.

sentences.zh: 靈運既東，與族弟惠連、東海何長瑜、潁川荀雍、泰山羊璿之以文章賞會，共為山澤之游，時人謂之四友。

translations.literal: Lingyun having gone east, with clansman younger brother Huilian, Donghai's He Changyu, Yingchuan's Xun Yong, and Taishan's Yang Xuanzhi he joined in literary appreciation and together roamed mountains and marshes; men of the time called them the Four Friends.
translations.idiomatic: Lingyun having gone east, with clansman Huilian, Donghai's He Changyu, Yingchuan's Xun Yong, and Taishan's Yang Xuanzhi he joined in literary appreciation and roamed mountains and marshes together; men of the time called them the Four Friends.

sentences.zh: 惠連幼有奇才，不為父方明所知。

translations.literal: Huilian from youth had extraordinary talent and was not known by his father Fangming.
translations.idiomatic: Huilian from childhood had extraordinary talent and was not known by his father Fangming.

sentences.zh: 靈運去永嘉還始甯，時方明為會稽，靈運造方明，遇惠連，大相知賞。

translations.literal: Lingyun left Yongjia and returned to Shining; at the time Fangming was in Kuaiji; Lingyun visited Fangming, met Huilian, and they greatly knew and prized each other.
translations.idiomatic: Lingyun left Yongjia and returned to Shining; Fangming was then in Kuaiji; Lingyun visited Fangming, met Huilian, and they greatly knew and prized each other.

sentences.zh: 靈運性無所推，唯重惠連，與為刎頸交。

translations.literal: Lingyun by nature pushed no one, yet especially valued Huilian and with him made a throat-cutting friendship.
translations.idiomatic: By nature Lingyun deferred to no one, yet he especially prized Huilian and with him made a throat-cutting friendship.

sentences.zh: 時何長瑜教惠連讀書，亦在郡內，靈運又以為絕倫。

translations.literal: At the time He Changyu taught Huilian to read and was also in the commandery; Lingyun also thought him unmatched.
translations.idiomatic: Then He Changyu taught Huilian to read and was also in the commandery; Lingyun also thought him unmatched.

sentences.zh: 謂方明曰：「阿連才悟如此，而尊作常兒遇之；

translations.literal: He said to Fangming, "A-Lian's talent and understanding are like this, yet you treat him as an ordinary child;
translations.idiomatic: "A-Lian's talent and understanding are like this, yet you treat him as an ordinary child;, he said to Fangming

sentences.zh: 長瑜當今仲宣，而飴以下客之食。

translations.literal: Changyu today is Zhongxuan, yet you feed him as a low guest.
translations.idiomatic: Changyu today is a Zhongxuan, yet you feed him as a low guest.

sentences.zh: 尊既不能禮賢，宜以長瑜還靈運。

translations.literal: You cannot treat the worthy with rites—you should return Changyu to Lingyun.
translations.idiomatic: Since you cannot treat the worthy with proper rites, you ought to return Changyu to Lingyun.

sentences.zh: 」載之而去。

translations.literal: He loaded him and went away.
translations.idiomatic: This man loaded him and went away.

sentences.zh: 荀雍字道雍，官至員外散騎郎。

translations.literal: Xun Yong, styled Daoyong, held office up to Extraordinary Gentleman of Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Yong, courtesy name Daoyong, rose to Extraordinary Gentleman of Scattered Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 璿之字曜璠，為臨川內史，被司空竟陵王誕所遇，誕敗坐誅。

translations.literal: Yang Xuanzhi, styled Yaofan, was Interior Administrator of Linchuan; he was favored by Minister of Works Prince Ziliang of Jingling; when the prince was defeated he was executed as associate.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xuanzhi, courtesy name Yaofan, was Interior Administrator of Linchuan; he was favored by Minister of Works Prince Ziliang of Jingling; when the prince was defeated he was put to death as associate.

sentences.zh: 長瑜才亞惠連，雍、璿之不及也。

translations.literal: Changyu's talent was next to Huilian; Yong and Xuanzhi did not match.
translations.idiomatic: Changyu's talent became next to Huilian; Yong and Xuanzhi did not match.

sentences.zh: 臨川王義慶招集文士，長瑜自國侍郎至平西記室參軍。

translations.literal: Prince Yiqing of Linchuan gathered literary men; Changyu went from State Attendant Gentleman to Recorder on the Pacification of the West staff.
translations.idiomatic: Changyu went from State Attendant Gentleman to Recorder on the Pacification of the West staff.; prince Yiqing of Linchuan gathered literary men

sentences.zh: 嘗于江陵寄書與宗人何勖，以韻語序義慶州府僚佐云：「陸展染白髮，欲以媚側室，青青不解久，星星行復出。

translations.literal: Once at Jiangling he sent a letter to clansman He Xun, using rhymed language to sequence Yiqing's provincial staff, saying, "Lu Zhan dyes white hair wanting to please the side chamber; green-green does not understand long-lasting—stars stars will again come out.
translations.idiomatic: Once at Jiangling he sent a letter to clansman He Xun, using rhymed language to sequence Yiqing's provincial staff: "Lu Zhan dyes white hair wanting to please the side chamber; green-green does not understand long-lasting—stars stars will again come out."

sentences.zh: 」如此者五六句。

translations.literal: Such were five or six lines.
translations.idiomatic: There were five or six such lines.

sentences.zh: 而輕薄少年遂演之，凡人士並為題目，皆加劇言苦句，其文流行。

translations.literal: Frivolous young men then expanded it; every gentleman was made a subject, all with harsh bitter lines added; the writing circulated.
translations.idiomatic: Frivolous young men then expanded it; every gentleman became made a subject, all with harsh bitter lines added; the writing circulated.

sentences.zh: 義慶大怒，白文帝，除廣州所統曾城令。

translations.literal: Yiqing was greatly angered, told Emperor Wen, and Changyu was sent out as Magistrate of Zengcheng under Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yiqing became greatly angered, told Emperor Wen, and Changyu was sent out as Magistrate of Zengcheng under Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 及義慶薨，朝士並詣第敘哀，何勖謂袁淑曰：「長瑜便可還也。

translations.literal: When Yiqing died, court gentlemen all went to the residence to express mourning; He Xun said to Yuan Shu, "Changyu can now return.
translations.idiomatic: After Yiqing died, court gentlemen all went to the residence to express mourning; He Xun said to Yuan Shu, "Changyu can now return.

sentences.zh: 」淑曰：「國新喪宗英，未宜以流人為念。

translations.literal: Shu said, "The state has newly lost its clan hero—it is not yet fitting to think of an exile.
translations.idiomatic: Shu said, "The state has just lost its pillar of the clan—it is not yet time to think of bringing back an exile."

sentences.zh: 」廬陵王紹鎮尋陽，以長瑜為南中郎行參軍，掌書記之任。

translations.literal: Prince Shao of Luling garrisoned Xunyang and made Changyu Army Registrar on the Central Army, in charge of secretarial duties.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Shao of Luling garrisoned Xunyang and appointed Changyu Army Registrar on the Central Army, putting him in charge of secretarial duties.

sentences.zh: 行至板橋，遇暴風溺死。

translations.literal: When the route reached Banqiao he met violent wind and drowned.
translations.idiomatic: At the time when the route reached Banqiao he met violent wind and drowned.

sentences.zh: 靈運因祖父之資，生業甚厚，奴僮既眾，義故門生數百，鑿山浚湖，功役無已。

translations.literal: Lingyun by his grandfather's resources had very thick livelihood; slaves and servants were many and retainers and gate students numbered in the hundreds; he dug mountains and dredged lakes—labor without end.
translations.idiomatic: Lingyun by his grandfather's resources lived in great wealth; slaves and servants were many and retainers and gate students numbered in the hundreds; he dug mountains and dredged lakes—labor without end.

sentences.zh: 尋山陟嶺，必造幽峻，岩嶂數十重，莫不備盡。

translations.literal: Seeking mountains and climbing ridges, he always reached secluded steep places; dozens of layers of cliffs and peaks—none were not fully explored.
translations.idiomatic: Seeking mountains and climbing ridges, he always reached secluded steep places; dozens of layers of cliffs and peaks—none went unexplored.

sentences.zh: 登躡常著木屐，上山則去其前齒，下山去其後齒。

translations.literal: Climbing he always wore wooden clogs; going up mountain he removed the front teeth, going down mountain the rear teeth.
translations.idiomatic: When climbing he always wore wooden clogs, removing the front teeth for ascent and the rear teeth for descent.

sentences.zh: 嘗自始甯南山伐木開徑，直至臨海，從者數百。

translations.literal: Once from Shining's southern mountains he cut timber and opened a path straight to Linhai; followers numbered in the hundreds.
translations.idiomatic: Followers numbered in the hundreds.; once from Shining's southern mountains he cut timber and opened a path straight to Linhai

sentences.zh: 臨海太守王琇驚駭，謂為山賊，末知靈運乃安。

translations.literal: Linhai Administrator Wang Xiu was alarmed and thought them mountain bandits; only when he learned it was Lingyun was he reassured.
translations.idiomatic: Linhai Administrator Wang Xiu became alarmed and thought them mountain bandits; only when he learned it was Lingyun was he reassured.

sentences.zh: 又要琇更進，琇不肯。

translations.literal: He again wanted Xiu to advance further; Xiu would not.
translations.idiomatic: This man again wanted Xiu to advance further; Xiu would not.

sentences.zh: 靈運贈琇詩曰：「邦君難地嶮，旅客易山行。

translations.literal: Lingyun gave Xiu a poem saying, "The state's lord finds the terrain perilous—the traveler finds mountain travel easy.
translations.idiomatic: Lingyun gave Xiu a poem: "The state's lord finds the terrain perilous—the traveler finds mountain travel easy.

sentences.zh: 」在會稽亦多從眾，驚動縣邑。

translations.literal: In Kuaiji too he often went with a crowd and alarmed the counties.
translations.idiomatic: In Kuaiji too he often traveled with a large party and alarmed the districts.

sentences.zh: 太守孟顗事佛精懇，而為靈運所輕，嘗謂顗曰：「得道應須慧業，丈人生天當在靈運前，成佛必在靈運後。

translations.literal: Administrator Meng Yi was earnest in Buddhist devotion yet was looked down on by Lingyun; he once told Yi, "Attaining the Way requires wisdom-karma; you, sir, will be born in heaven before Lingyun, yet become Buddha after Lingyun.
translations.idiomatic: Administrator Meng Yi was earnest in Buddhist devotion yet was looked down on by Lingyun; he once told Yi, "Attaining the Way requires wisdom-karma; you, sir, will be born in heaven before Lingyun, yet become Buddha after Lingyun."

sentences.zh: 」顗深恨此言。

translations.literal: Yi deeply resented these words.
translations.idiomatic: Yi deeply resented the remark.

sentences.zh: 又與王弘之諸人出千秋亭飲酒，裸身大呼，顗深不堪，遣信相聞。

translations.literal: Again with Wang Hongzhi and others he went out to the Thousand Autumns Pavilion to drink; naked he shouted loudly; Yi could not bear it and sent a messenger with word.
translations.idiomatic: Naked he shouted loudly; again with Wang Hongzhi and others he went out to the Thousand Autumns Pavilion to drink

sentences.zh: 靈運大怒曰：「身自大呼，何關癡人事。」

translations.literal: Lingyun was greatly angered and said, "I myself shout loudly—what business is it of foolish men?
translations.idiomatic: "I myself shout loudly—what business is it of foolish men?, lingyun was greatly angered and said

sentences.zh: 會稽東郭有回踵湖，靈運求決以為田，文帝令州郡履行。

translations.literal: East of Kuaiji's outer city was Huizong Lake; Lingyun sought to open it for fields; Emperor Wen ordered the province and commanderies to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: East of Kuaiji's outer city was Huizong Lake; Lingyun sought to drain it for fields; Emperor Wen ordered the province and commanderies to investigate.

sentences.zh: 此湖去郭近，水物所出，百姓惜之，顗堅執不與。

translations.literal: This lake was near the city; aquatic products came from it; common people cherished it; Yi firmly would not give it.
translations.idiomatic: This lake became near the city; aquatic products came from it; common people cherished it; Yi firmly would not give it.

sentences.zh: 靈運既不得回踵，又求始寧休崲湖為田，顗又固執。

translations.literal: Lingyun not obtaining Huizong, again sought Shining's Xiqi Lake for fields; Yi again firmly resisted.
translations.idiomatic: Denied Huizong, Lingyun again sought to drain Shining's Xiqi Lake for fields; Yi again firmly resisted.

sentences.zh: 靈運謂顗非存利人，政慮決湖多害生命，言論傷之。

translations.literal: Lingyun said Yi did not store up benefit for people but only feared draining lakes would harm many lives; his talk wounded him.
translations.idiomatic: His talk wounded him.; lingyun said Yi did not store up benefit for people but only feared draining lakes would harm many lives

sentences.zh: 與顗遂隙。

translations.literal: With Yi he then had a rift.
translations.idiomatic: He and Yi then fell out.

sentences.zh: 因靈運橫恣，表其異志，發兵自防，露板上言。

translations.literal: Because Lingyun was overbearing and willful, Yi memorialized his rebellious intent, raised troops for self-defense, and proclaimed on an exposed board.
translations.idiomatic: Because Lingyun became overbearing and willful, Yi memorialized his rebellious intent, raised troops for self-defense, and proclaimed on an exposed board.

sentences.zh: 靈運馳詣闕上表，自陳本末。

translations.literal: Lingyun galloped to the palace and submitted a memorial stating the sequence from beginning to end.
translations.idiomatic: Lingyun rode posthaste to the palace and submitted a memorial explaining the whole affair from start to finish.

sentences.zh: 文帝知其見誣，不罪也。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen knew he was slandered and did not punish him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen knew he became slandered and did not punish him.

sentences.zh: 不欲復使東歸，以為臨川內史。

translations.literal: Not wishing to send him east again, he was made Interior Administrator of Linchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Not wishing to send him east again, he became made Interior Administrator of Linchuan.

sentences.zh: 在郡遊放，不異永嘉，為有司所糾。

translations.literal: In the commandery he roamed freely no different from Yongjia and was impeached by the relevant offices.
translations.idiomatic: In the commandery he roamed freely no different from Yongjia and became impeached by the relevant offices.

sentences.zh: 司徒遣使隨州從事鄭望生收靈運。

translations.literal: The Minister of Education sent an envoy with the provincial aide Zheng Wangsheng to seize Lingyun.
translations.idiomatic: That Minister of Education sent an envoy with the provincial aide Zheng Wangsheng to seize Lingyun.

sentences.zh: 靈運興兵叛逸，遂有逆志。

translations.literal: Lingyun raised troops and rebelled in flight; then he had rebellious intent.
translations.idiomatic: Then he had rebellious intent.; lingyun raised troops and rebelled in flight

sentences.zh: 為詩曰：「韓亡子房奮，秦帝魯連恥，本自江海人，忠義感君子。

translations.literal: He composed a poem saying, "Han fell and Zifang rose, Qin Emperor—Lu Lian's shame; originally men of rivers and seas, loyalty and righteousness move the noble man.
translations.idiomatic: This man composed a poem saying, "Han fell and Zifang rose, Qin Emperor—Lu Lian's shame; originally men of rivers and seas, loyalty and righteousness move the noble man.

sentences.zh: 」追討禽之，送廷尉，廷尉論正斬刑。

translations.literal: Pursued and captured, he was sent to the Court of Judicial Review; the Court of Judicial Review judged death by decapitation.
translations.idiomatic: Pursued and captured, he became sent to the Court of Judicial Review; the Court of Judicial Review judged death by decapitation.

sentences.zh: 上愛其才，欲免官而已。

translations.literal: The Emperor loved his talent and wished only to dismiss him from office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor loved his talent and wished only to dismiss him from office.

sentences.zh: 彭城王義康堅執，謂不宜恕。

translations.literal: Prince Yikang of Pengcheng firmly held that he should not be pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yikang of Pengcheng held firm that he ought not be pardoned.

sentences.zh: 詔以「謝玄勳參微管，宜宥及後嗣，降死徙廣州」。

translations.literal: An edict said, "Xie Xuan's merit participated in subtle governance; favor should extend to later generations; death reduced—banished to Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said, "Xie Xuan's merit participated in subtle governance; favor should extend to later generations; death reduced—banished to Guangzhou."

sentences.zh: 後秦郡府將宋齊受使至塗口，行達桃墟村，見有七人下路聚語，疑非常人，還告郡縣，遣兵隨齊掩討禽之。

translations.literal: Later Qin Commandery garrison commander Song Qi, on mission to Tukou, on the road reached Taoxu Village and saw seven men leave the road gathering to talk; he suspected they were not ordinary men, returned and told the commandery and county, and troops followed Qi to seize them.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward, Qin Commandery garrison commander Song Qi, on mission to Tukou, on the road reached Taoxu Village and saw seven men leave the road gathering to talk; he suspected they were not ordinary men, returned and told the commandery and county, and troops followed Qi to seize them.

sentences.zh: 其一人姓趙名欽，云：「同村薛道雙先與靈運共事，道雙因同村成國報欽云：'靈運犯事徙廣州，給錢令買弓箭刀楯等物，使道雙要合鄉里健兒于三江口篡之。

translations.literal: One man surnamed Zhao named Qin said, "Fellow villager Xue Daoshuang first worked with Lingyun; Daoshuang through fellow villager Chen Guo told Qin: 'Lingyun offended and was banished to Guangzhou, gave money ordering purchase of bows, arrows, blades, shields, and the like, and had Daoshuang gather stalwart men of the village at Sanjiangkou to seize him.
translations.idiomatic: One man surnamed Zhao named Qin said, "Fellow villager Xue Daoshuang first worked with Lingyun; Daoshuang through fellow villager Chen Guo told Qin: 'Lingyun offended and was exiled to Guangzhou, gave money ordering purchase of bows, arrows, blades, shields, and the like, and had Daoshuang gather stalwart men of the village at Sanjiangkou to seize him.

sentences.zh: 若得志如意後，功勞是同。

translations.literal: If ambition is attained as wished afterward, merit and labor are the same.
translations.idiomatic: If their ambition was afterward attained as they wished, merit and labor would be shared alike.

sentences.zh: 遂合部党要謝不得，及還饑饉，緣路為劫。

translations.literal: They then combined a faction to waylay Xie but could not; on return there was famine and along the road they turned to robbery.'"
translations.idiomatic: They then combined a faction to waylay Xie but could not; on return there became famine and along the road they turned to robbery.'"
