sentences.zh: '」有司奏收之，文帝詔于廣州棄市。

translations.literal: The relevant offices memorialized to seize him; Emperor Wen's edict was execution by public display in Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: That relevant offices memorialized to seize him; Emperor Wen's edict was execution by public display in Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 臨死作詩曰：「龔勝無餘生，李業有終盡，嵇公理既迫，霍生命亦殞。

translations.literal: Facing death he composed a poem saying, "Gong Sheng had no surplus life, Li Ye had final end; Ji Kang's principle was already pressed, Huo's life also perished.
translations.idiomatic: Facing death he composed a poem: "Gong Sheng had no surplus life, Li Ye had final end; Ji Kang's principle was already pressed, Huo's life also perished."

sentences.zh: 」所稱龔勝、李業，猶前詩子房、魯連之意也。

translations.literal: The Gong Sheng and Li Ye he named still carried the intent of Zifang and Lu Lian in the earlier poem.
translations.idiomatic: That Gong Sheng and Li Ye he named still carried the intent of Zifang and Lu Lian in the earlier poem.

sentences.zh: 時元嘉十年，年四十九。

translations.literal: At the time it was the tenth year of Yuanjia; he was forty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: Then it was the tenth year of Yuanjia; he was forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 所著文章傳於世。

translations.literal: Writings he composed circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: The writings he left circulated in the world.

sentences.zh: 孟顗字彥重，平昌安丘人，衛將軍昶弟也。

translations.literal: Meng Yi, styled Yanzhong, was a man of Anqiu in Pingchang, younger brother of General of the Guard Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Yi, courtesy name Yanzhong, came from Anqiu in Pingchang, younger brother of General of the Guard Chang.

sentences.zh: 昶、顗並美風姿，時人謂之雙珠。

translations.literal: Chang and Yi both had fine bearing; men of the time called them twin pearls.
translations.idiomatic: Men of the time called them twin pearls.; chang and Yi both had fine bearing

sentences.zh: 昶貴盛，顗不就辟。

translations.literal: Chang was noble and flourishing; Yi did not accept summons.
translations.idiomatic: Chang became noble and flourishing; Yi did not accept summons.

sentences.zh: 昶死後，顗曆侍中、僕射、太子詹事、散騎常侍、左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: After Chang died, Yi held posts in succession as Palace Attendant, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Grand Warden of the Heir Apparent, Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, and Left Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: After Chang died, Yi rose step by step to Palace Attendant, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Grand Warden of the Heir Apparent, Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, and Left Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 嘗就徐羨之因敘關、洛中事，顗歎劉穆之終後便無繼者，王弘亦在，甚不平，曰：「昔魏朝酷重張合，謂不可一日無之。

translations.literal: Once visiting Xu Xianzhi he narrated affairs of Guan and Luo; Yi sighed that after Liu Muzhi's end there was no successor; Wang Hong was also present and very displeased, saying, "In old days Wei heavily valued Zhang He and said one day could not be without him.
translations.idiomatic: Once visiting Xu Xianzhi he narrated affairs of Guan and Luo; Yi sighed that after Liu Muzhi's end there was no successor; Wang Hong was also present and very displeased: "In old days Wei heavily valued Zhang He and said one day could not be without him.

sentences.zh: 及合死，何關興廢？

translations.literal: When He died, what did it matter to rise and fall?
translations.idiomatic: What did it matter to rise and fall?, when He died

sentences.zh: 」顗不悅，眾賓笑而釋之。

translations.literal: Yi was displeased; the assembled guests laughed and released the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Yi became displeased; the assembled guests laughed and released the matter.

sentences.zh: 後卒于會稽太守。

translations.literal: Later he died as Administrator of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward, he died as Administrator of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 靈運子鳳，坐靈運徙嶺南，早卒。

translations.literal: Lingyun's son Feng, because Lingyun was banished to Lingnan, died young.
translations.idiomatic: Lingyun's son Feng, because Lingyun was exiled to Lingnan, died young.

sentences.zh: 謝超宗

translations.literal: Xie Chaozong
translations.idiomatic: Xie Chaozong

sentences.zh: 鳳子超宗。

translations.literal: Feng's son Chaozong.
translations.idiomatic: Feng's son was Chaozong.

sentences.zh: 隨父鳳嶺南，元嘉末得還。

translations.literal: Following his father Feng to Lingnan, at the end of Yuanjia he was able to return.
translations.idiomatic: Following his father Feng to Lingnan, at the end of Yuanjia he became able to return.

sentences.zh: 與慧休道人來往。

translations.literal: He associated with the monk Hui Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: This man associated with the monk Hui Xiu.

sentences.zh: 好學有文辭，盛得名譽。

translations.literal: He loved learning and had literary skill; he quickly won great reputation.
translations.idiomatic: This man loved learning and had literary skill; he quickly won great reputation.

sentences.zh: 選補新安王子鸞國常侍。

translations.literal: Selected and appointed State Attendant Gentleman to Prince Luan of Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: He was chosen and made State Attendant Gentleman to Prince Luan of Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 王母殷淑儀卒，超宗作誄奏之，帝大嗟賞，謂謝莊曰：「超宗殊有鳳毛，靈運復出。

translations.literal: When the Prince's mother Lady Yin Shuyi died, Chaozong composed the eulogy and presented it; the Emperor greatly sighed in praise and told Xie Zhuang, "Chaozong especially has phoenix down—Lingyun born again.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince's mother Lady Yin Shuyi died, Chaozong composed the eulogy and presented it; the Emperor greatly sighed in praise and told Xie Zhuang, "Chaozong especially has phoenix down—Lingyun born again."

sentences.zh: 」時右衛將軍劉道隆在御坐，出候超宗曰：「聞君有異物，可見乎？

translations.literal: At the time General of the Right Guard Liu Daolong was in the imperial seat; he went out to wait on Chaozong and said, "I hear you have a rare thing—may I see it?
translations.idiomatic: Then General of the Right Guard Liu Daolong was in the imperial seat; he went out to wait on Chaozong and said, "I hear you have a rare thing—may I see it?

sentences.zh: 」超宗曰：「懸磬之室，復有異物邪。

translations.literal: Chaozong said, "A house with empty bells—again a rare thing?
translations.idiomatic: "A house with empty bells—again a rare thing?, chaozong said

sentences.zh: 」道隆武人無識，正觸其父名，曰：「旦侍宴，至尊說君有鳳毛。

translations.literal: Daolong was a military man without understanding; he exactly touched his father's name and said, "At tomorrow's banquet the Supreme One said you have phoenix down.
translations.idiomatic: Daolong was a military man without understanding; he exactly touched his father's name and said, "At tomorrow's banquet the Supreme One said you have phoenix down."

sentences.zh: 」超宗徒跣還內。

translations.literal: Chaozong went barefoot back inside.
translations.idiomatic: Chaozong went back inside barefoot.

sentences.zh: 道隆謂檢覓鳳毛，至闇待不得，乃去。

translations.literal: Daolong meant to search for phoenix down; he waited in the dark and could not get it, then left.
translations.idiomatic: Daolong meant to search for phoenix down; he waited in the dark, failed to get it, and left.

sentences.zh: 泰始中，為尚書殿中郎。

translations.literal: In the Taishi era he was Gentleman of the Palace Department of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taishi era he became Gentleman of the Palace Department of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 三年，都令史駱宰議策秀孝格，五問並得為上，四三為中，二為下，一不第。

translations.literal: In the third year, Chief Clerk of the Capital Luo Zai debated the standards for the provincial and filial selection examination: five questions all correct counts as upper, four or three as middle, two as lower, one as failure.
translations.idiomatic: In year three, Capital Chief Clerk Luo Zai debated standards for the provincial and filial selection examination: five questions all correct counts as upper, four or three as middle, two as lower, one as failure.

sentences.zh: 超宗議不同，詔從宰議。

translations.literal: Chaozong's debate differed; an edict followed Zai's debate.
translations.idiomatic: An edict followed Zai's debate.; chaozong's debate differed

sentences.zh: 齊高帝為領軍，愛其才，衛將軍袁粲聞之，謂高帝曰：「超宗開亮，善可與語。

translations.literal: Emperor Gao of Qi as General Who Leads the Army loved his talent; General of the Guard Yuan Can heard and told the Emperor Gao, "Chaozong is open and bright—one can talk with him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gao of Qi as General Who Leads the Army loved his talent; General of the Guard Yuan Can heard and told Gao, "Chaozong is open and bright—one can talk with him.

sentences.zh: 」取為長史、臨淮太守。

translations.literal: He was taken as Chief Clerk and Administrator of Linhuai.
translations.idiomatic: This man was taken as Chief Clerk and Administrator of Linhuai.

sentences.zh: 粲誅，高帝以超宗為義興太守。

translations.literal: When Can was executed, Gao made Chaozong Administrator of Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: When Can was put to death, Gao made Chaozong Administrator of Yixing.

sentences.zh: 升明二年，坐公事免。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shengming he was dismissed for public affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Shengming year two he was dismissed for public affairs.

sentences.zh: 詣東府門自通，其日風寒，高帝謂四座曰：「此客至，使人不衣自暖矣。

translations.literal: He came to the Eastern Headquarters gate and announced himself; that day the wind was cold; Gao told those seated, "This guest arriving makes one need no clothes to feel warm.
translations.idiomatic: This man came to the Eastern Headquarters gate and announced himself; that day the wind was cold; Gao told those seated, "This guest arriving makes one need no clothes to feel warm.

sentences.zh: 」超宗既坐，飲酒數杯，辭氣橫出，高帝對之甚歡。

translations.literal: Chaozong having sat, after several cups of wine his words and spirit crossed outward; Gao facing him was very pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Chaozong having sat, after several cups his words and spirit crossed outward; Gao facing him was very pleased.

sentences.zh: 及齊受禪，為黃門郎。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication he was Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: At the time when Qi received the abdication he was Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 有司奏撰郊廟歌，上敕司徒褚彥回、侍中謝朏、散騎侍郎孔珪、太學博士王咺之、總明學士劉融、何法圖、何曇秀作者凡十人，超宗辭獨見用。

translations.literal: The relevant offices memorialized to compose suburban and temple hymns; the Emperor ordered Minister of Education Chu Yanzhi, Palace Attendant Xie Tiao, Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry Kong Gui, Grand Master of the National University Wang Xuanzhi, and Generalists of Total Brightness Liu Rong, He Fatu, and He Tanxiu—ten authors in all; Chaozong's composition alone was used.
translations.idiomatic: The relevant offices memorialized to compose suburban and temple hymns; the Emperor ordered Minister of Education Chu Yanzhi, Palace Attendant Xie Tiao, Regular Attendant Kong Gui, National University Grand Master Wang Xuanzhi, and Total Brightness generalists Liu Rong, He Fatu, and He Tanxiu—ten authors in all; Chaozong's composition alone was used.

sentences.zh: 為人恃才使酒，多所陵忽，在直省常醉。

translations.literal: As a man he relied on talent and urged wine, often slighting others; in direct attendance at the office he was often drunk.
translations.idiomatic: As a man he relied on talent and urged wine, often slighting others; in direct attendance at the office he became often drunk.

sentences.zh: 上召見，語及北方事，超宗曰：「虜動來二十年矣，佛出亦無如之何。

translations.literal: The Emperor summoned him and spoke of northern affairs; Chaozong said, "The barbarians have been on the move for twenty years—even Buddha coming out could do nothing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned him and spoke of northern affairs; Chaozong said, "The barbarians have been on the move for twenty years—even Buddha coming out could do nothing.

sentences.zh: 」以失儀出為南郡王中軍司馬。

translations.literal: For loss of decorum he was sent out as Army Major to Prince Jun of Nan.
translations.idiomatic: For loss of decorum he became sent out as Army Major to Prince Jun of Nan.

sentences.zh: 人問曰：「承有朝命，定是何府？

translations.literal: Someone asked, "I hear there is a court order—what office is it?
translations.idiomatic: "I hear there is a court order—what office is it?, someone asked

sentences.zh: 」超宗怨望，答曰：「不知是司馬，為是司驢；

translations.literal: Chaozong resentful answered, "I don't know whether it is Major or Donkey;
translations.idiomatic: Chaozong answered resentfully, "I don't know whether it is Major or Donkey;

sentences.zh: 既是驢府，政應為司驢。

translations.literal: since it is the Donkey headquarters, properly it should be Donkey Major.
translations.idiomatic: Since it is the Donkey headquarters, the post ought properly to be Donkey Major.

sentences.zh: 」為有司奏，以怨望免，禁錮十年。

translations.literal: The relevant offices memorialized; for resentment he was dismissed and confined for ten years.
translations.idiomatic: That relevant offices memorialized; for resentment he was dismissed and confined for ten years.

sentences.zh: 後司徒褚彥回因送湘州刺史王僧虔，閣道壞，墜水；

translations.literal: Later Minister of Education Chu Yanzhi because he was seeing off Xiang Province Inspector Wang Sengqian—the gallery road collapsed and he fell into the water;
translations.idiomatic: Later Minister of Education Chu Yanzhi, seeing off Xiang Inspector Wang Sengqian—the gallery road collapsed and he fell into the water;

sentences.zh: 僕射王儉驚跣下車。

translations.literal: Vice Director Wang Jian in alarm ran barefoot from the carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Wang Jian, startled, leapt barefoot from the carriage.

sentences.zh: 超宗拊掌笑曰：「落水三公，墜車僕射。

translations.literal: Chaozong clapped hands and laughed, "Water-fallen Three Duke, carriage-fallen Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Chaozong clapped his hands and laughed, "Water-fallen Three Duke, carriage-fallen Vice Director."

sentences.zh: 」彥回出水，沾濕狼藉。

translations.literal: Yanzhi came out of the water, soaked and in disarray.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhi climbed out of the water, soaked and in disarray.

sentences.zh: 超宗先在僧虔舫，抗聲曰：「有天道焉，天所不容，地所不受。

translations.literal: Chaozong was earlier on Sengqian's boat and called out loudly, "There is Heaven's Way—Heaven will not contain it, Earth will not receive it.
translations.idiomatic: Chaozong was earlier on Sengqian's boat and called out loudly, "There is Heaven's Way—Heaven will not contain it, Earth will not receive it."

sentences.zh: 投畀河伯，河伯不受。

translations.literal: Cast to the River Lord—the River Lord will not receive.
translations.idiomatic: Cast upon the River Lord—and the River Lord would not receive him.

sentences.zh: 」彥回大怒曰：「寒士不遜。

translations.literal: Yanzhi greatly angered said, "Cold-house man without deference.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhi said in great anger, "Cold-house man without deference.

sentences.zh: 」超宗曰：「不能賣袁、劉得富貴，焉免寒士。

translations.literal: Chaozong said, "Cannot sell Yuan and Liu to get wealth and honor—how avoid cold-house man.
translations.idiomatic: Chaozong said, "Cannot sell Yuan and Liu to get wealth and honor—how avoid cold-house man?"

sentences.zh: 」前後言誚，稍布朝野。

translations.literal: Before and after, words of mockery gradually spread through court and countryside.
translations.idiomatic: Before long such words of mockery gradually spread through court and countryside.

sentences.zh: 武帝即位，使掌國史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu took the throne he had him manage the state history.
translations.idiomatic: At the time when Emperor Wu took the throne he had him manage the state history.

sentences.zh: 除竟陵王征北諮議，領記室，愈不得志。

translations.literal: He was made Staff Officer to Prince Jingling's Pacification of the North and Recorder; he was ever more without ambition.
translations.idiomatic: He became Staff Officer to Prince Jingling's Pacification of the North and Recorder; he was ever more without ambition.

sentences.zh: 超宗為子娶張敬兒女為婦，帝甚疑之。

translations.literal: Chaozong had his son marry Zhang Jing'er's daughter; the Emperor greatly suspected this.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor greatly suspected this.; chaozong had his son marry Zhang Jing'er's daughter

sentences.zh: 及敬兒誅，超宗謂丹陽尹李安人曰：「往年殺韓信，今年殺彭越，君欲何計？

translations.literal: When Jing'er was executed Chaozong told Acting Governor of Danyang Li Anren, "Last year Han Xin was killed, this year Peng Yue—what plan do you have?
translations.idiomatic: When Jing'er was executed Chaozong told Acting Danyang Governor Li Anren, "Last year Han Xin was killed, this year Peng Yue—what plan do you have?

sentences.zh: 」安人具啟之。

translations.literal: Anren fully reported this.
translations.idiomatic: Anren reported the whole matter.

sentences.zh: 上積懷超宗輕慢，使兼中丞袁彖奏超宗請付廷尉。

translations.literal: The Emperor's accumulated resentment at Chaozong's lightness had Associate Censor-in-Chief Yuan Yan memorialize to hand Chaozong to the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: That Emperor's accumulated resentment at Chaozong's lightness had Associate Censor-in-Chief Yuan Yan memorialize to hand Chaozong to the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 武帝雖可其奏，以彖言辭依違，使左丞王逡之奏彖「輕文略奏，撓法容非，請免彖所居官」。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu though approving the memorial, because Yan's words were hedging, had Left Assistant Director Wang Junzhi memorialize that Yan "treats writing lightly and omits the memorial, bends law to tolerate wrong—request dismissal from Yan's office.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu though approving the memorial, because Yan's words were hedging, had Left Assistant Director Wang Junzhi memorialize that Yan "treats writing lightly and omits the memorial, bends law to tolerate wrong—request dismissal from Yan's office."

sentences.zh: 詔「彖匿情欺國，愛朋罔主，免官，禁錮十年」。

translations.literal: Edict: "Yan hides feeling and deceives the state, loves partisans and misleads the lord—dismissed from office, confined ten years.
translations.idiomatic: Edict: "Yan hides feeling and deceives the state, loves partisans and misleads the lord—dismissed from office, confined ten years."

sentences.zh: 超宗下廷尉，一宿發白皓首。

translations.literal: Chaozong sent down to the Court of Judicial Review; in one night his hair turned white.
translations.idiomatic: In one night his hair turned white.; chaozong sent down to the Court of Judicial Review

sentences.zh: 詔徙越嶲，行至豫章，上敕豫章內史虞悰賜盡，勿傷其形骸。

translations.literal: Edict banishment to Yuexi; on the road reaching Yuzhang, the Emperor ordered Yuzhang Interior Administrator Yu Cong to grant death—do not harm the bodily frame.
translations.idiomatic: Banishment was ordered to Yuexi; on the road at Yuzhang the emperor commanded Yuzhang Interior Administrator Yu Cong to grant death—without harming the bodily frame.

sentences.zh: 明年，超宗門生王永先又告超宗子才卿死罪二十餘條。

translations.literal: The next year Chaozong's gate student Wang Yongxian again reported Chaozong's son Caiqing guilty of capital crimes in more than twenty articles.
translations.idiomatic: That next year Chaozong's gate student Wang Yongxian again reported Chaozong's son Caiqing guilty of capital crimes in more than twenty articles.

sentences.zh: 上疑其妄，以才卿付廷尉辯，以不實見原。

translations.literal: The Emperor suspected it false and handed Caiqing to the Court of Judicial Review to debate; for untruth he was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor suspected it false and handed Caiqing to the Court of Judicial Review to debate; for untruth he was pardoned.

sentences.zh: 永先於獄盡之。

translations.literal: Yongxian was executed in prison.
translations.idiomatic: Yongxian became executed in prison.

sentences.zh: 謝幾卿

translations.literal: Xie Jiqing
translations.idiomatic: Xie Jiqing

sentences.zh: 才卿弟幾卿，清辯，時號神童。

translations.literal: Caiqing's younger brother Jiqing—clear in debate, at the time called a divine child.
translations.idiomatic: Caiqing's younger brother Jiqing was clear in debate and at the time called a divine child.

sentences.zh: 超宗徙越嶲，詔家人不得相隨。

translations.literal: When Chaozong was banished to Yuexi, an edict said family members could not follow.
translations.idiomatic: When Chaozong was exiled to Yuexi, an edict said family members could not follow.

sentences.zh: 幾卿年八歲，別父于新亭，不勝其慟，遂投于江。

translations.literal: Jiqing was eight years old; parting from his father at Xinting he could not bear the grief and threw himself into the river.
translations.idiomatic: Jiqing became eight years old; parting from his father at Xinting he could not bear the grief and threw himself into the river.

sentences.zh: 超宗命估客數人入水救之，良久湧出，得就岸，瀝耳目口鼻，出水數斗，十餘日乃裁能言。

translations.literal: Chaozong ordered several merchant travelers into the water to save him; after long time he bubbled up; brought to shore they drained ears, eyes, mouth, and nose—several pecks of water; more than ten days before he could barely speak.
translations.idiomatic: Chaozong ordered several merchant travelers into the water to save him; after a long time he bubbled up; brought to shore they drained ears, eyes, mouth, and nose—several pecks of water; more than ten days before he could barely speak.

sentences.zh: 居父憂哀毀過禮。

translations.literal: In mourning for his father his grief and ruin exceeded the rites.
translations.idiomatic: In mourning for his father he grieved and wasted himself beyond the rites.

sentences.zh: 年十二，召補國子生。

translations.literal: At twelve he was summoned and appointed student of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: At twelve he was called up and appointed student of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 齊文惠太子自臨策試，謂王儉曰：「幾卿本長玄理，今可以經義訪之。

translations.literal: Prince Wenhui of Qi personally came to examine by question; he told Wang Jian, "Jiqing originally excels in dark principle—now one may inquire of him on classic meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Wenhui of Qi personally came to examine by question and told Wang Jian, "Jiqing originally excels in dark principle—now one may inquire of him on classic meaning."

sentences.zh: 」儉承旨發問，幾卿辯釋無滯，文惠大稱賞焉。

translations.literal: Jian received the intent and raised questions; Jiqing argued and explained without obstruction; Wenhui greatly praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Jiqing argued and explained without obstruction; jian received the intent and raised questions

sentences.zh: 儉謂人曰：「謝超宗為不死矣。

translations.literal: Jian told people, "Xie Chaozong is not dead.
translations.idiomatic: Jian told people, "Xie Chaozong is not dead."

sentences.zh: 」及長，博學有文采。

translations.literal: When grown he was broadly learned and had literary color.
translations.idiomatic: When grown he was widely learned and had literary color.

sentences.zh: 仕齊為大尉晉安王主簿。

translations.literal: He served Qi as Chief Clerk to the Grand Marshal Prince Jin'an.
translations.idiomatic: This man served Qi as Chief Clerk to the Grand Marshal Prince Jin'an.

sentences.zh: 梁天監中，自尚書三公郎為書侍御史。

translations.literal: In the Tianjian era of Liang he went from Gentleman of the Three Masters of Writing to Writing Attendant Censor.
translations.idiomatic: In Liang's Tianjian era he went from Gentleman of the Three Masters of Writing to Writing Attendant Censor.

sentences.zh: 舊郎官轉為此職者，世謂之南奔。

translations.literal: Old custom: when a Gentleman transferred to this post the world called it fleeing south.
translations.idiomatic: By old custom, when a Gentleman was transferred to this post men called it "fleeing south."

sentences.zh: 幾卿頗失志，多陳疾，台事略不復理。

translations.literal: Jiqing was quite without ambition; he often claimed illness and barely managed office affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Jiqing became quite without ambition; he often claimed illness and barely managed office affairs.

sentences.zh: 累遷尚書左丞。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 幾卿詳悉故實，僕射徐勉每有凝滯，多詢訪之。

translations.literal: Jiqing knew old precedents in detail; Vice Director Xu Mian whenever he had blockage often inquired of him.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Xu Mian whenever he had blockage often inquired of him.; jiqing knew old precedents in detail

sentences.zh: 然性通脫，會意便行，不拘朝憲。

translations.literal: Yet his nature was free and unrestrained; when the intent struck he acted— not bound by court law.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his nature became free and unrestrained; when the intent struck he acted— not bound by court law.

sentences.zh: 嘗預樂游苑宴，不得醉而還，因詣道邊酒壚，停車褰幔，與車前三騶對飲。

translations.literal: Once he attended a banquet at Leyou Garden, could not get drunk and returned; he then went to a wine shop by the road, stopped the carriage, lifted the curtain, and with the three outriders before the carriage faced each other drinking.
translations.idiomatic: Once, after a banquet at Leyou Garden where he could not get drunk, he stopped at a wine shop by the road, lifted the carriage curtain, and drank facing the three outriders before the carriage.

sentences.zh: 時觀者如堵，幾卿處之自若。

translations.literal: At the time onlookers were like a wall; Jiqing handled it at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Then onlookers were like a wall; Jiqing handled it at ease.

sentences.zh: 後以在省署夜著犢鼻褌，與門生登閣道飲酒酣呼，為有司糾奏，坐免。

translations.literal: Later because in the office at night he wore calf-nose breeches and with gate students climbed the gallery path drinking deeply and shouting loudly, he was impeached by the relevant offices and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward, because in the office at night he wore calf-nose breeches and with gate students climbed the gallery path drinking deeply and shouting loudly, he was impeached by the relevant offices and dismissed.

sentences.zh: 普通六年，詔西昌侯藻督眾軍北侵，幾卿啟求行，擢為藻軍師長史。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Putong an edict had Marquis Xi of Xichang supervise the armies on northern invasion; Jiqing memorialized asking to go and was promoted to Chief Clerk and Army Major on Xi's staff.
translations.idiomatic: In Putong year six an edict had Marquis Xi of Xichang supervise the armies on northern invasion; Jiqing memorialized asking to go and was promoted to Chief Clerk and Army Major on Xi's staff.

sentences.zh: 將行，與僕射徐勉別，勉云：「淮、淝之役，前謝已著奇功，未知今謝何如？

translations.literal: About to leave he parted from Vice Director Xu Mian; Mian said, "On the Huai and Fei campaign the earlier Xie already showed strange merit—I do not know how the present Xie will be?
translations.idiomatic: "On the Huai and Fei campaign the earlier Xie already showed strange merit—I do not know how the present Xie will be?, about to leave he parted from Vice Director Xu Mian; Mian said

sentences.zh: 」幾卿應聲曰：「已見今徐勝於前徐，後謝何必愧于前謝。

translations.literal: Jiqing answered at once, "I already see the present Xu surpasses the earlier Xu—the later Xie why must be ashamed before the earlier Xie?
translations.idiomatic: Jiqing answered at once, "I already see the present Xu surpasses the earlier Xu—the later Xie need not be ashamed before the earlier Xie."

sentences.zh: 」勉默然。

translations.literal: Mian was silent.
translations.idiomatic: Mian fell silent.

sentences.zh: 軍至渦陽退敗，幾卿坐免官。

translations.literal: When the army reached Guoyang and retreated in defeat, Jiqing was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: When the army reached Guoyang and retreated in defeat, Jiqing was removed from office.

sentences.zh: 居白楊石井宅，朝中交好者載酒從之，客恒滿坐。

translations.literal: He lived at the White Poplar Stone Well residence; friends at court loaded wine and followed him—guests always filled the seats.
translations.idiomatic: This man lived at the White Poplar Stone Well residence; friends at court loaded wine and followed him—guests always filled the seats.

sentences.zh: 時左丞庾仲容亦免歸，二人意相得，並肆情誕縱，或乘露車歷遊郊野，醉則執鐸輓歌，不屑物議。

translations.literal: At the time Left Assistant Director Yu Zhongrong was also dismissed and returned; the two men's intent matched; together they gave free rein to wild excess—sometimes riding an open carriage roaming the suburbs and fields; drunk then holding a bell and singing elegies, disdaining worldly opinion.
translations.idiomatic: Then Left Assistant Director Yu Zhongrong was also dismissed and returned; the two men's intent matched; together they gave free rein to wild excess—sometimes riding an open carriage roaming the suburbs and fields; drunk then holding a bell and singing elegies, disdaining worldly opinion.

sentences.zh: 湘東王繹在荊鎮與書慰勉之。

translations.literal: Prince Yi of Xiangdong at his Jing garrison wrote to comfort and encourage him.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yi of Xiangdong, garrisoning Jing, wrote to comfort and encourage him.

sentences.zh: 後為太子率更令。

translations.literal: Later he was Director of the Crown Prince's Office of Rate Regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward, he was Director of the Crown Prince's Office of Rate Regulation.

sentences.zh: 放達不事容儀。

translations.literal: Free and unrestrained, he did not attend to appearance.
translations.idiomatic: Free and unrestrained, he paid no heed to appearance.

sentences.zh: 性不容非，與物多忤，有乖己者，輒肆意罵之，退無所言。

translations.literal: His nature could not tolerate wrong; with things he often clashed; whoever went against him he at once freely reviled, and afterward said nothing.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he could not tolerate wrong; he often clashed with others, and whoever crossed him he would revile freely—then fall silent afterward.

sentences.zh: 遷左丞。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Left Assistant Director.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Left Assistant Director.

sentences.zh: 僕射省嘗議集公卿，幾卿外還，宿醉未醒，取枕高臥，傍若無人。

translations.literal: The Vice Director's office once deliberated gathering dukes and ministers; Jiqing returned from outside, still drunk from overnight, took a pillow and slept high—beside him as though no one.
translations.idiomatic: That Vice Director's office once deliberated gathering dukes and ministers; Jiqing returned from outside, still drunk from overnight, took a pillow and slept high—beside him as though no one.

sentences.zh: 又嘗於閣省裸袒酣飲，及醉小遺，下沾令史，為南司所彈，幾卿亦不介意。

translations.literal: Again once in the office pavilion he drank naked and drunk, and drunk made small urination that dripped down on the clerks; impeached by the Southern Bureau, Jiqing also did not mind.
translations.idiomatic: Again, once in the office pavilion he drank naked and, drunk, urinated on the clerks below; impeached by the Southern Bureau, Jiqing did not mind at all.

sentences.zh: 轉左光祿長史。

translations.literal: He transferred to Chief Clerk to the Left Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: He moved on to Chief Clerk to the Left Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 卒，文集行於世。

translations.literal: He died; collected writings circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: This man died; collected writings circulated in the world.

sentences.zh: 幾卿雖不持檢操，然於家門篤睦。

translations.literal: Though Jiqing did not hold himself to restraint, yet within the family gate he was deeply harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: Though Jiqing did not hold himself to restraint, yet within the family gate he became deeply harmonious.

sentences.zh: 兄才卿早卒，子藻幼孤，幾卿撫養甚至。

translations.literal: Elder brother Caiqing died young; son Zao was young and orphaned; Jiqing raised and nurtured him with utmost care.
translations.idiomatic: Elder brother Caiqing died young; son Zao became young and orphaned; Jiqing raised and nurtured him with utmost care.

sentences.zh: 及藻成立，歷清官，皆幾卿獎訓之力也。

translations.literal: When Zao was established, holding pure offices—all was Jiqing's reward and instruction.
translations.idiomatic: When Zao came of age and held pure offices, it was all through Jiqing's encouragement and teaching.

sentences.zh: 論曰：謝晦以佐命之功，當顧托之重，殷憂在日，黜昏啟聖，于社稷之計，蓋為大矣。

translations.literal: Discussion says: Xie Hui by merit in founding the dynasty, at the weight of entrustment in regency, with deep grief in daily affairs, deposed the dim and opened the sage—for the state's plan it was indeed great.
translations.idiomatic: The discussion runs: Xie Hui, by merit in founding the dynasty and at the weight of regency entrustment, with deep grief in daily affairs, deposed the dim and opened the sage—for the state's plan it was indeed great.

sentences.zh: 但廬陵之殞，事非主命，昌門之覆，有乖臣道。

translations.literal: Yet Prince Luling's death was not the lord's command; the overturning at Chang Gate went against the minister's way.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Prince Luling's death became not the lord's command; the overturning at Chang Gate went against the minister's way.

sentences.zh: 博陸所慎，理異於斯。

translations.literal: What the Marquis of Boling cautioned—reason differed from this.
translations.idiomatic: What the Marquis of Boling had warned against rested on different reasoning.

sentences.zh: 加以身處上流，兵權總己，將欲以外制內，豈人主所久堪乎。

translations.literal: Add that he himself held the upper reaches and military power totaled to himself; wishing to use outside to control inside—how could a lord long endure it?
translations.idiomatic: Wishing to use outside to control inside—how could a lord long endure it?; add that he himself held the upper reaches and military power totaled to himself

sentences.zh: 向令徐、傅不亡，道濟居外，四權制命，力足相侔，劉氏之危，則有逾累卵。

translations.literal: If Xu and Fu had not died and Daoji held the outside, four powers commanding fate with strength enough to match each other—the Liu house's peril would have exceeded piled eggs.
translations.idiomatic: Had Xu and Fu not died and Daoji remained outside, four powers commanding fate with strength enough to balance one another—the Liu house's peril would have exceeded piled eggs.

sentences.zh: 以此論罰，豈曰妄誅。

translations.literal: By this to discuss punishment—how can one say reckless execution?
translations.idiomatic: Judged by this, the punishment can hardly be called reckless execution.

sentences.zh: 宣遠所為寒心，可謂睹其萌矣。

translations.literal: What Xuanyuan did made the heart cold—one may say he saw the sprout.
translations.idiomatic: What Xuanyuan did would chill the heart—he had already seen the first sprout.

sentences.zh: 然謝氏自晉以降，雅道相傳，景恒、景仁以德素傳美，景懋、景先以節義流譽。

translations.literal: Yet the Xie clan from Jin onward transmitted elegant conduct; Jingheng and Jingren by plain virtue transmitted beauty; Jingmao and Jingxian by integrity and righteousness streamed reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Yet from Jin onward the Xie clan handed down refined ways; Jingheng and Jingren won praise through plain virtue, Jingmao and Jingxian through integrity and righteousness.

sentences.zh: 方明行己之度，玄暉藻繢之奇，各擅一時，可謂德門者矣。

translations.literal: Fangming's measure in conducting himself, Xuanhui's marvel in ornamentation—each excelled in its age; they can be called a house of virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Fangming's standard in conduct, Xuanhui's brilliance in ornament—each mastered an age; together they may be called a house of virtue.

sentences.zh: 靈運才名，江左獨振；

translations.literal: Lingyun's talent and fame uniquely shook the Jiangzuo;
translations.idiomatic: Lingyun's talent and fame shook the Jiangzuo as none other had;

sentences.zh: 而猖獗不已，自致覆亡。

translations.literal: yet overbearing without end, he brought ruin on himself.
translations.idiomatic: yet rampaging without end, he brought ruin on himself.

sentences.zh: 人各有能，茲言乃信，惜乎！

translations.literal: Each man has his capacity—this saying is indeed true; alas!
translations.idiomatic: Each man has his gift—this saying holds true; what a pity!
